title: ops: guidebook parity sweep — reagent effects, cooking appliance, plant metabolism, entity stats, reactions
description: ## Context Our static guidebook is live at `https://ss14.zig.computer/guidebook/`, rendered daily by `vs14-guidebook-build.service` running `ops/guidebook/render.py` (1,824 lines). It handles 6 embed types from the SS14 `Resources/ServerInfo/Guidebook/*.xml` content, turning in-game guidebook XMLs into static HTML with sprite + recipe + tech tables (vs-1e5, vs-mlg, vs-3o7). User audit: the tables **drop content that's present in the source YAML**. Examples called out: - Food recipes don't say what tools/appliances they use. - Chemicals don't have their effects shown. - Plant metabolism effects are invisible. This bead is the parity sweep: research what's missing, /spec the fixes, /review OQs, /test, /impl. --- ## PARITY SWEEP — what's rendered now vs what should be ### `GuideReagentEmbed` + `GuideReagentGroupEmbed` **Rendered today** (per `_reagent_row`, render.py:833–853): - Swatch (color) - Name (Fluent-resolved) - Description (Fluent-resolved) **Missing from source YAML**: - **Group** — `Medicine` / `Toxin` / `Biological` / `Narcotic` / `Drink` / `Food` / `Admin` etc. Category matters for understanding "is this a med or a street drug." - **Bloodstream effects** — the entire `metabolisms.Bloodstream.effects` array. Today we lose: - `EvenHealthChange` heals/damages (e.g. Bicaridine heals 1.5 Brute/tick) - `HealthChange` damages under OD conditions (Bicaridine does 0.5 Asphyxiation + 1.5 Poison above 15u) - `Vomit` / `Jitter` / `Drowsiness` / `Stun` status effects with OD threshold conditions - `ModifyBloodLevel`, `Polymorph`, `SlurSpeech`, etc. - **OD / safety thresholds** — implicit in `ReagentCondition.min` values on effects. E.g. "Bicaridine overdoses at 15u → Asphyxiation damage; at 30u → vomiting with 2% chance per tick." This is derivable from the effect conditions and is HUGE for in-game safety. - **Metabolism rate** — declared in `metabolisms.Bloodstream.metabolismRate` or inherited default. Determines how quickly the reagent ticks down (and how fast it heals). - **Plant metabolism** — `plantMetabolism.effects` array. Reagents like Ammonia, Saltpeter, Robust Harvest, Weed Killer, Ash all affect plants differently. Botanists need this; chemistry dept can reference it. - **Physical description** — `physicalDesc` Fluent key ("opaque," "refreshing," "reflective"). Minor but reveals clues to poisoners + flavor. - **Flavor text** — `flavor` key (taste descriptor). - **Reactions that produce this reagent** — currently the guidebook doesn't cross-reference to synthesis. Knowing "Bicaridine = O + C + Sugar" inline saves a trip. ### `GuideMicrowaveGroupEmbed` (cooking recipes) **Rendered today** (render.py:911–969): - Result (dish name) - Recipe (dish name, capitalized) - Inputs (reagents + solids) - Time (seconds) **Missing**: - **Appliance** — column never present. It's implied by `GuideMicrowaveGroupEmbed` = microwave-only, but the column itself should say "Microwave" explicitly so users can scan "what tool do I need." Future-proofs when we add other cooking embeds. - **Temperature requirements** — some recipes may have them? Check the prototype schema. - **Other cooking recipe types** — `type: microwaveMealRecipe` is the ONLY recipe type `render.py` loads (see `load_microwave_recipes`). SS14 in its current base may also have: - Slicing recipes (cut bread with a knife → bread slices) - Grill/oven recipes (not sure if these exist in the pure SS14 base we rebuilt on; verify) - Construction recipes (`type: construction`, `type: constructionGraph` — 4× hits grep'd — these render building flows, probably not "food" but worth checking) - **Recipe requires a reaction beforehand** — e.g. a dish that needs "prepared dough" which itself is a reagent reaction. Cross-link to Chemistry would help. ### `GuideTechDisciplineEmbed` (tech research) Need to audit `_render_tech_discipline_embed` (render.py:970–1014) for what it shows vs what the YAML has. Not audited here — include in research pass. ### `GuideLawsetListEmbed` (AI lawsets) Need to audit `_render_lawset_list_embed` (render.py:1038–1061) similarly. Probably fine but worth a look. ### `GuideEntityEmbed` (entities — mobs, objects, structures) **Rendered today**: sprite `` (vs-mlg) + caption. Plus a fallback pill if sprite missing. **Missing**: - **Stats** — entity prototypes often have: - `MaxHealth` / `DamageContainer` / damage resistance / armor modifiers - `SolutionContainerManagerComponent` capacity (for beakers, syringes: size in units) - `StorageComponent` capacity (bags, boxes) - `SpeciesSpawnComponent` details (for mob species entities) - These would enrich the embed from "picture + name" to "picture + name + stat block." ### Reactions (not currently rendered at all) The chemistry-reaction data (~300 reactions across `Resources/Prototypes/Recipes/Reactions/**/*.yml`) has **NO guidebook embed type**. Reagent pages don't link to their recipes. **Proposed**: `GuideReactionEmbed` and `GuideReactionGroupEmbed` — per-reaction card (reactants + catalysts + products + temperature + impact). Caveat: Nurseshark's `/reactions` surface does this more interactively. The guidebook equivalent should be static and printable. Both could coexist — each deep-links to the other. ### Plants / produce / seeds Hydroponics content (seeds, produce, plant stats — yield, endurance, potency, harvest window) may not have a guidebook embed. If it does, verify completeness. If not, that's a parity miss worth filing. --- ## /SPEC — proposed fixes ### Phase 1 — reagent effects in the table (highest user-visible value) Extend `_reagent_row` + the reagent-table schema: Current columns: `[Color+Name] [Desc]` Proposed columns: `[Color+Name] [Group] [Desc] [Effects] [Thresholds]` - **Effects** cell: render the Bloodstream + Plant metabolism effect arrays as bullets. Handle known types: - `EvenHealthChange` / `HealthChange` → "heals 1.5 Brute/tick" / "deals 0.5 Asphyxiation above 15u" - `GenericStatusEffect` → "grants Adrenaline for 120s" - `Jitter` / `Vomit` / `Drowsiness` / `Stun` / `SlurSpeech` → "jitters above 15u," etc. - `ModifyBloodLevel` → "restores +20% blood volume" - `PlantAdjustHealth` / `PlantAdjustWeed` / etc. → "boosts plant yield by 0.1," "kills weeds" - Unknown types: `{type}: {keys}` pass-through so new effects don't vanish silently - **Thresholds** cell: derive "OD at X" from the smallest `ReagentCondition.min` value that introduces damage or bad effects; "Safe" if none; "Unknown" if data missing. Show just the number (e.g. "OD 15u"). - Keep single-reagent embeds (`GuideReagentEmbed`) as a detail view (all columns, maybe vertical layout); use condensed columns on group tables (`GuideReagentGroupEmbed`) to stay scan-able. ### Phase 2 — cooking appliance column + other recipe types Extend `_render_microwave_group_embed` + add siblings: - **Add `Appliance` column** to microwave recipe table. Hardcoded "Microwave" for now; becomes real when we add other types. - **Support additional cooking prototype types**: - Verify which exist in the pure SS14 base: `sliceableFood`, `reaction` (for dough / sauces), `constructionRecipe`? - Add loaders for each, emit embeds `GuideSlicingGroupEmbed`, `GuideReactionRecipeGroupEmbed` (or whatever convention fits). File stubs for types that don't currently have usage; doesn't cost bandwidth to render what exists. - Cross-link: if a recipe's ingredient is itself a reagent/reaction, link the ingredient name to its reagent page. ### Phase 3 — plant metabolism (parallel with Phase 1 since it shares the effects-rendering code) Ship the plant-effect rendering subset of Phase 1. Dedicated section on each reagent's row for plant-side effects, visually differentiated (e.g. leaf icon). ### Phase 4 — entity stat blocks Extend `GuideEntityEmbed` (when sprite is shown) to include a collapsible stats block. Default-collapsed so the layout doesn't break existing content; one-click expand to see: - Max HP (if `DamageContainer` has one) - Container capacity (beakers, syringes, storage) - Armor modifiers - Species info (for mob prototypes that use `species` field) ### Phase 5 — reactions embed (new capability) Add `GuideReactionEmbed` and `GuideReactionGroupEmbed` for per-reaction cards (reactants + catalysts + products + minTemp + impact). Not required for parity — EXTENDS the guidebook's reach. **Out of scope for this bead** if it grows the work too much — file as vs-3cj.X-follow-up. ### Phase 6 — audit pass for remaining gaps Enumerate the guidebook's XML tree and make a spreadsheet / markdown table of every `` vs what's in the source prototype. Anything that the in-game client shows richer than our static site, flag for fix. --- ## Acceptance ### Phase 1 - [ ] Reagent tables include Group column - [ ] Reagent tables include Effects cell with all effect types rendered (not silently dropped for unknown types) - [ ] Reagent tables include Thresholds cell (OD value or "Safe") - [ ] Single-reagent embeds show richer vertical layout with every effect - [ ] Plant metabolism effects present where applicable - [ ] `ops/guidebook/render.py` unit-tested for the new extraction helpers (at least one fixture per effect type) ### Phase 2 - [ ] Microwave recipe table gains Appliance column - [ ] Other cooking types (verified to exist) get their own embed renderers - [ ] Recipe ingredient names link to reagent pages when applicable ### Phase 3, 4, 5 (may split into follow-up beads if scope grows) ### Phase 6 (ongoing) - [ ] Parity audit document at `docs/guidebook-parity.md` — table of every embed type + what it renders + what's dropped + status --- ## Open Questions (for /review) ### OQ-1: Scope — all phases in this bead, or split? Phase 1 (reagent effects) is the highest-value fix. Phase 2 (appliance/cooking) is mid-value. 4 (stat blocks) and 5 (reactions embed) are scope-growers. Options: - **All phases, one bead** (this spec) — long runway, ships comprehensive parity. - **Phase 1 only in this bead**, file 2/3/4/5 as follow-ups — faster to ship the most-impactful fix; incremental. My bias: Phase 1 + Phase 2 + Phase 3 in this bead (shared rendering code). Phases 4 and 5 as follow-ups. ### OQ-2: Effect rendering — interpretive vs literal? Two approaches for the Effects cell: - **Literal** — dump the effect type + damage numbers in a compact form: "EvenHealthChange Brute -1.5 · HealthChange Asphyxiation 0.5 Poison 1.5 @Reagent≥15u." - **Interpretive** — translate to plain English: "heals 1.5 brute per tick; above 15u it also does 0.5 asphyxiation and 1.5 poison." - Interpretive is more readable but harder to keep accurate (needs mapping logic for every effect type). Literal is ugly but mechanically true. My bias: interpretive for the well-known types (`HealthChange`, `Jitter`, `Vomit`, `ModifyBloodLevel`, `PlantAdjustHealth`), literal fallback for anything unknown. Keeps the common case readable. ### OQ-3: OD threshold detection — conservative or exact? Multiple effects can have different `ReagentCondition.min` values (Bicaridine: 15u for Asphyxiation damage, 30u for Vomit). Options: - **Single "OD at X"** — use the smallest value that introduces a negative effect. Conservative; tells you when to stop pushing. - **Progressive** — "15u: asphyxiation damage; 30u: vomit; 45u: blood-level modification." Full picture; more text. My bias: show the smallest as the primary "OD at X" value in the compact column, expand to full progressive list in the single-reagent detail view. ### OQ-4: Sibling tool cross-linking Guidebook is one of our three data-tools (guidebook / cookbook / nurseshark). Should reagent embeds in the guidebook link out to: - Nurseshark's reagent detail page (`/nurseshark/reagents/`)? - Cookbook recipes that use this reagent (for cooking ingredients)? - Both via a small "Related tools" footer? My bias: ship the "Related tools" footer. Low cost, high utility. Needs confirmed URL patterns before rolling in. ### OQ-5: Layout — table growth strategy Adding 2-3 columns to the reagent table will cramp mobile viewports. Options: - **Responsive collapse** — on narrow widths, collapse to name + group + expand-chevron that opens detail. - **Scrollable table** — horizontal scroll on narrow widths. - **Two-row rendering** — primary row + secondary row with effects / thresholds. My bias: responsive collapse. Already standard on our stack. ### OQ-6: Who runs the audit doc? Phase 6 — `docs/guidebook-parity.md` spreadsheet. I can generate it during the /impl phase, OR a separate /review-time artifact that informs future fixes. My bias: /impl generates it as a side effect of the sweep. Living doc; each phase updates it. --- ## Dependencies - No hard blockers — render.py is standalone - vs-1e5, vs-mlg, vs-3o7 (all CLOSED) — prior guidebook work; this builds on it ## Priority P2 — player-facing correctness + utility. Not blocking any launch gate, but gaps-vs-in-game-reality is a credibility issue for the first-party tooling. ## Out of scope - In-game guidebook client changes (that's upstream's territory) - Multi-language / i18n for effect descriptions (Fluent system already resolves names; effect explanations ship in English) - Rebuilding the guidebook in React/TS (render.py is adequate; replacing its stack is a separate rebuild bead, not a parity fix) --- ## WIKI LANGUAGE REFERENCE (post-/review incorporation) User direction: "use [the wiki] for the guidebook language (interpretive english should reference this to see how base game words stuff -- we are still equal w base game)." Four canonical pages to mirror voice from: - https://wiki.spacestation14.com/wiki/Medical - https://wiki.spacestation14.com/wiki/Guide_to_Medical - https://wiki.spacestation14.com/wiki/Reagents - https://wiki.spacestation14.com/wiki/Medicine ### Voice conventions from the wiki (apply to /impl) **Unit-rate phrasing:** - "Bicaridine is the best basic option for healing straight brute damage, healing 2 brute damage per unit." - "Dermaline will heal 4.5 (1.5 cold, shock, and heat respectively) damage per unit." - "Ointment ... will heal 15 points of damage, 5 in each category, per use." - "Epinephrine ... will counteract any further damage, as well as heal asphyxiation damage." Pattern: "X heals Y DamageType per unit" or "X heals Y1 Type1, Y2 Type2, Y3 Type3 per use." Avoid "deals 2 healing" style awkwardness. **OD / safe-dose phrasing:** - "Take extra care to not overdose too much, as it's maximum safe dose is 10u." - "the syringe's maximum amount is 15u" Surface OD thresholds as "maximum safe dose is Xu" not "OD: Xu" — matches the wiki's clearer framing. **Warnings:** - "'''Mixing any of these brute chemicals, ''including'' Bicaridine, will create Razorium''', a chemical that can cause even more brute damage than what you're trying to treat." - "However, Dermaline will not treat caustic damage. For this, you must use Sigynate, or Siderlac." Use strong-voice warnings with bold + colored callouts for harm-causing interactions; qualify exceptions inline. **Species-specific (do NOT drop this):** - "If the patient is an arachnid, note that Iron is toxic to them. Use Copper instead, which will provide the same effect to them." - Vox need nitrogen internals, 30s O2 tolerance, 2-minute recovery window. - Moth iron-metabolism exception (insect blood). - Diona sap blood + Robust Harvest healing. ### Additional facts to fold into rendered content - **Critical-only heals**: "Epinephrine does technically heal Brute, Burn, and Poison damage categories, but only when in a critical state." Surface this as a footnote on Epinephrine's card. - **Below-50-damage condition**: "Tricordrazine only works below 50 total damage." Footnote. - **Defibrillator numbers**: "a defibrillator can be used to heal up to 40 asphyxiation damage while applying 5 units of shock damage." Include in Airloss section. - **Bloodloss threshold**: "If your blood level falls below a certain threshold(<90%), you will begin taking bloodloss damage." Show on Bloodloss page. - **Revival threshold**: "ensure that their Total Damage is below 200 points by using Topical Treatments" before defib. - **Stasis bed side effects**: 10× slower metabolism, asphyxiates living patients, topicals still work. Worth a dedicated cryo-adjacent callout. - **Medipen contents**: 15u total, contains Epinephrine + 3u Tranexamic Acid. - **Syringe mechanics**: right-click to change dose (5/10/15u); Z to switch draw/inject. - **CMO hypospray**: 30u capacity, 5u doses, instant injection. ### Inspirations list update Added to Nurseshark README + CLAUDE.md already (commit 90299ed in nurseshark). Guidebook (this project) gets the wiki added to the renderer's docstring header in the /impl phase.
close_reason: Guidebook parity Phase 1+2+3 shipped at commit 94cbac5f (merged via 88aecea6). render.py +1077 lines. Reagent group tables now 5 columns (Name/Group/Desc/Effects/Thresholds); single-reagent embeds become vertical cards with progressive threshold ladder + Nurseshark 'Related tools' footer. 40+ effect types interpretively rendered in wiki voice (heals X, max safe dose Xu). Plant metabolism section with leaf-tag pill. Microwave recipes gain Appliance column. Metamorph recipes loaded for future use. docs/guidebook-parity.md living audit doc. 8/8 new tests pass. Phase 4 (entity stat blocks) + Phase 5 (reactions embed) deferred to follow-up beads per spec.

title: feat: guidebook entity stat blocks — MaxHealth, capacity, armor on GuideEntityEmbed (Phase 4 of vs-05o)
description:
## Context
vs-05o Phase 4. Subagent's recommendation from the closing report:

"Scope: collapsible `<details>` under each entity sprite showing MaxHealth (read from `MobStateThresholds` / `DamageContainer` components with parent-chain walk), `SolutionContainerManager` capacity (for beakers / syringes / pill canisters), `Storage` capacity (bags / boxes), `PowerCell` charge, armor multipliers from `Armor` / `ClothingSpeedModifier`.

Complication: SS14 components inherit across the parent chain just like Sprite does — reuse `_walk_parents`.

Acceptance: every `GuideEntityEmbed` of a mob / container / equipment renders at least one stat row; pure-decorative entities remain sprite-only.

Effort estimate: 1 session, ~400 lines. ~15 new entity loader extensions."

## Scope
Extend `ops/guidebook/render.py` `GuideEntityEmbed` handler:
- Parse entity prototypes for stat components (MobStateThresholds, DamageContainer, SolutionContainerManager, Storage, PowerCell, Armor, ClothingSpeedModifier)
- Reuse `_walk_parents()` for component inheritance
- Render a collapsible `<details>` block with stat rows under the sprite
- Pure-decorative entities (no stat components) remain sprite-only
- Update `docs/guidebook-parity.md` to reflect GuideEntityEmbed's status change from Partial → Full

## Acceptance
- [ ] Every mob-category GuideEntityEmbed shows MaxHealth + damage resistance
- [ ] Every container-category GuideEntityEmbed shows capacity
- [ ] Every clothing-category GuideEntityEmbed shows Armor + slowdown if present
- [ ] Pure-decorative entities unchanged
- [ ] 2+ new pytest cases

## Priority
P2. Finishes the vs-05o epic's "entity stat blocks" milestone.

## Dispatch
Well-scoped worktree subagent. ~1 session.
close_reason: Entity stat blocks shipped at commit 38aea0fd79. GuideEntityEmbed gains collapsible <details> stat table when entity has meaningful stats. 222 stat blocks across 1040 embeds (decorative-entity filter suppresses 617 sparse 1-row blocks). Coverage: MobThresholds (max_health, crit_threshold), Damageable, SolutionContainerManager (food/drink/tank/lube/beaker/welder/pen/etc. capacity), Storage (slots + max item size), Battery (max + starting charge), Armor (per-DamageType coefficients), ClothingSpeedModifier + MovementSpeedModifier (walk/sprint tiles/s). Parent-chain inheritance via _walk_parents. 22/22 pytest pass (9 new). Deviations: decorative filter for entities whose only stat would be damage container; added MovementSpeedModifier for mob speed (bead listed only ClothingSpeedModifier but mob-side analog wasn't surfaced otherwise).

title: feat: guidebook reactions embed — GuideReactionEmbed/Group + reagent 'produced by' cross-link (Phase 5 of vs-05o)
description:
## Context
vs-05o Phase 5. Subagent's recommendation from the closing report:

"Scope: new XML tags `GuideReactionEmbed` (single) + `GuideReactionGroupEmbed`, new loader `load_reactions` for `type: reaction` under `Resources/Prototypes/Recipes/Reactions/**/*.yml` (~300 reactions), loader also builds a reverse index `reagent → reactions that produce it` used by Phase 1 reagent detail cards.

Cross-link: each reagent's detail card gains 'Produced by' section listing reactions.

Mixer requirement: reactions can require a specific mixer entity (beaker / chem dispenser) — render that as a tool hint.

Temperature / catalyst rendering matters; effect type `ChemVomit` etc. on reactions also reuses Phase 1's `_render_effect`.

Acceptance: full reaction cards, bidirectional cross-links with reagent embeds, 300+ reactions indexed.

Effort estimate: 1–2 sessions."

## Scope
1. New embed types in `ops/guidebook/render.py`:
   - `GuideReactionEmbed` — single reaction card (reactants, catalysts, products, minTemp/maxTemp, impact, mixer hint)
   - `GuideReactionGroupEmbed` — grouped reaction table (e.g. "all brute-med synthesis")
2. `load_reactions()` loader indexing `type: reaction` prototypes from `Resources/Prototypes/Recipes/Reactions/**/*.yml`
3. Reverse index: `reagent_id → reactions_producing_it[]`, used to enrich Phase 1's reagent detail cards with a "Produced by" section
4. Cross-link bidirectionality: reactions link to their output reagent's page; reagents link to their producing reactions
5. Tool hint: if a reaction requires a specific mixer (detectable via YAML structure), render it
6. Update `docs/guidebook-parity.md` — GuideReaction* rows flip from "None" to "Full"

## Acceptance
- [ ] ~300 reactions rendered via group embed
- [ ] Single reaction embed usable standalone in guidebook XML
- [ ] Reagent detail cards gain "Produced by" cross-link section
- [ ] Temperature + catalyst + mixer rendered where present
- [ ] 3+ new pytest cases

## Priority
P2. Largest remaining guidebook gap — reactions are ~300 data points currently not surfaced.

## Dispatch
Well-scoped. 1-2 sessions. Blocks on vs-05o.1 (Phase 4 entity stats) only if both touch the same pytest fixtures.
close_reason: Reactions embed shipped at worktree commit 18a4500ec7; merged into main via 40c1e66da1. 313 reactions indexed, 37 temp-gated, 12 catalyzed, 75 mixer-required, 39 with side-effects. 265 reagents gain 'Produced by' cross-link section. New GuideReactionEmbed + GuideReactionGroupEmbed types. Reaction group derived from YAML filename (case-insensitive match). Catalysts distinct from reactants; not counted in reverse index. 33/33 pytest pass (11 new). docs/guidebook-parity.md: GuideReaction* rows Full. XML wire-up of new tags in Resources/ServerInfo/Guidebook/Chemistry.xml is a separate small content PR (flagged in parity doc deferred section).

title: ci: audit stale.yml behavior on VS14's tiny issue set
description:
## Context
`.github/workflows/stale.yml` runs daily (`0 0 * * *`). Latest run:
success. Unlike the other scheduled workflows, this one is doing
something — it uses `actions/stale@v9` to mark untriaged issues/PRs
stale after 90 days of inactivity.

```yaml
days-before-stale: 90
remove-stale-when-updated: true
only-issue-labels: 'S: Untriaged'
stale-issue-label: 'Stale'
days-before-issue-close: -1      ← never auto-close
```

## Why this needs assessment (not urgent but worth a look)
1. **It acts on our issues / PRs with real consequences**. Unlike
   the others, a misconfiguration here would spam stale labels on
   random tickets.
2. **VS14 has ~0 issues open right now**, so its impact is currently
   nil — but the moment we have any bug reports, they're subject to
   this automation.
3. **Upstream's label vocabulary** (`S: Untriaged`, `Stale`) was
   imported from Delta-V/SS14. If we haven't created those labels,
   the workflow quietly no-ops. Could be fine, or could silently
   mask that we should be triaging things.
4. **`days-before-issue-close: -1` = never close** is a safe
   default, but we should confirm we want that behavior (vs the
   more common "warn at 60, close at 90" pattern).

## Task
1. Check which labels currently exist in the repo
   (`gh label list --repo azigler/vacation-station-14`).
2. Create `S: Untriaged` and `Stale` if missing; otherwise the
   workflow is just a no-op every night.
3. Decide: keep "warn only, never close" (current), or adopt
   "close after N days" semantics.
4. Document the chosen policy in `CONTRIBUTING.md` or similar so
   people understand what triggers the Stale label.

## Options
### Option A: keep as-is + create labels
Current behavior is safe and matches SS14 convention. Just make
sure the labels exist so it's not a silent no-op.

### Option B: tune the thresholds
30 / 60 / 90 days depending on what fits the project cadence.

### Option C: disable
If we don't want any automation acting on our issue tracker.

## Recommendation
**A**. Create the labels (5-minute task), leave the behavior
alone, document it.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `S: Untriaged` and `Stale` labels exist in the repo
- [ ] Decision recorded on thresholds / close semantics
- [ ] CONTRIBUTING.md has a Triage Policy note
- [ ] Next scheduled run completes without action-required warnings
notes: SCOPE CHANGE post-Flavor-A: stale.yml is Delta-V-invented, NOT in SS14 upstream. Post-reset it'll be removed. Re-scope: decide whether to RE-INTRODUCE stale issue management via a VS14-authored workflow. Current scope (label audit) is moot because the labels won't be auto-referenced without the workflow.

title: impl: adapt SS14 grafana dashboards for VS14
description:
## Context
SS14 community provides two Grafana dashboards as JSON exports:
- Game Servers (uid K0LTdKmMk): fleet overview
- Perf Metrics (uid qyFqpFiGk): per-server deep dive with Logs panel

Source: docs.spacestation14.com/en/community/infrastructure-reference/grafana-dashboards.html

## Dependencies
- vs-2p3 (prometheus/loki/grafana stack) must be running

## Task
Adapt the upstream SS14 dashboards for Vacation Station. Store JSON in repo.
Provision automatically on Grafana startup via provisioning.

## Acceptance Criteria

### Download and adapt
- [ ] Fetch raw dashboard JSON from docs page
- [ ] Store at ops/grafana/dashboards/game-servers.json
- [ ] Store at ops/grafana/dashboards/perf-metrics.json

### Adaptations
- [ ] Replace datasource UIDs with our Grafana's
- [ ] Verify `job="gameservers"` matches our Prometheus scrape config
- [ ] Verify `server` label values match (our instance name)
- [ ] Rename where appropriate (e.g. "Wizden Servers" -> "Vacation Station")

### Provisioning
- [ ] ops/grafana/provisioning/datasources/datasources.yml
- [ ] ops/grafana/provisioning/dashboards/dashboards.yml with file provider
  pointing at /var/lib/grafana/dashboards/
- [ ] docker-compose mounts dashboards + provisioning into Grafana container
- [ ] On fresh Grafana startup, both dashboards auto-appear

### Verification
- [ ] Game Servers dashboard shows our instance
- [ ] Perf Metrics dashboard's $Server variable populated with our instance name
- [ ] Logs panel on Perf Metrics shows live Loki logs
- [ ] Connections panel works (requires Postgres datasource configured)

### Documentation
- [ ] docs/OPERATIONS.md dashboard section
- [ ] Customization notes (where to edit for fork-specific metrics)
- [ ] How to add new panels or dashboards

human: advertise vacation-station on ss14 public hub
description:
## Context
Vacation Station 14 runtime config disables hub advertisement by default.
Players can still connect via direct URL (`ss14://51.81.33.136:1212`), but
the server won't appear in any launcher's public browser. Flip only when
ready for cold inbound traffic.

## Pre-flip checklist
- [ ] Run is stable: server has survived multiple full rounds without
      watchdog restart / crash-loop.
- [ ] Admin toolkit: at least one admin account seeded in postgres; admin
      commands (kick/ban/announce) tested from the client.
- [ ] **Rules & MOTD written** (see vs-rules bead) — hub launch with blank
      or upstream-default rules is a bad first impression.
- [ ] Auth decision made: flip to `mode = 1` (Required) before advertising
      unless you're consciously running a guest-friendly server. Guests
      via hub = grief farm in practice.
- [ ] vs-2y8 done (watchdog behind Caddy+HTTPS) — hub moderators and
      curious players will probe `:5000` and see plain HTTP.
- [ ] Discord crash alerts: `Notification.DiscordWebhook` populated in
      `/opt/ss14-watchdog/appsettings.yml` so we know when the server
      falls over.
- [ ] Capacity: enough resource headroom for first-wave hub traffic
      (recent metrics: tick rate, entity count, RSS under load). Cold
      starts from the hub can be 30+ players within minutes.

## Task — when ready
### Decide the hub list
Default SS14 hub: `hub.spacestation14.io` (Wizards Den). Adding additional
hubs is a comma-separated value in `hub.hub_urls`. Candidate hubs:

1. **Wizards Den** — `https://hub.spacestation14.io/` (primary, always include)
2. **Delta-V** — if Delta-V runs a distinct community hub, include it. VERIFY
   before listing. As of fork time we didn't confirm. Delta-V's server list
   lives somewhere public — check deltavstation.com or their Discord for
   the hub URL. If Delta-V uses Wizden hub only, skip.
3. **Starlight / other downstream communities** — some fork communities
   cross-list. Research before committing.
4. **Our own hub** — medium-term; we may eventually stand up a VS14-flavored
   hub that lists us plus sibling forks. Separate bead.

Multi-hub is free (each POST is independent) and discoverability-positive.
Being listed only on one hub means your server is invisible to clients
using other launchers configured against different hubs.

### Execute
1. Edit `/opt/ss14-watchdog/instances/vacation-station/config.toml`, find
   `[hub]` section.
2. Flip `advertise = true` (check the exact cvar name against the current
   template — might be `hub.advertise` or just `advertise` within the
   section).
3. Set `hub_urls` to the comma-separated list of hubs chosen above.
4. Confirm `server_url` is correct (the URL clients connect to after
   clicking through the browser). For now: `ss14://51.81.33.136:1212`.
   Once you have a domain, flip to `ss14://vacation.yourdomain.com:1212`.
5. Optionally set `tags` — e.g. `18+ rp-lite medium-pop hard-fork` — for
   launcher-side filtering.
6. Trigger server restart:
   ```
   curl -sS -u "vacation-station:$API_TOKEN" -X POST \
     https://<watchdog-url>/instances/vacation-station/restart
   ```
7. Verify:
   - Public SS14 launcher → server browser → "Vacation Station" appears
     within ~60s on each hub you listed.
   - Direct connect still works.
   - No hub-related errors in `journalctl -u ss14-watchdog --since '2 min ago'`.
   - Each hub's server list shows you at the expected tier (new, low-pop
     = sorted near bottom; that's normal).

### First-hour watch
Hub-new-server discovery wave can be 20-50 concurrent connections in the
first hour. Watch Grafana's Perf Metrics dashboard for tick rate drops,
entity count spikes, memory pressure. Be ready to flip Advertise back off
and POST /restart if the server's unstable.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `hub.advertise = true` on the live host
- [ ] `hub.hub_urls` populated with every hub we want to list on
- [ ] Server visible in the SS14 launcher's public browser on each hub
      within ~5 minutes
- [ ] `server.rules` / `server.motd` populated and sensible
- [ ] At least one active admin account defined in postgres
- [ ] First-hour watch complete; no restart storm, no OOM, tick rate stable
- [ ] Record flip timestamp + launch-day traffic notes in this bead

## Delisting risk — read before flipping
The Wizden hub has a moderation team that can DELIST your server for:
- Inadequate rules / MOTD
- Obvious grief / no-RP angle
- Harassment or discriminatory content in server identity
- Impersonating another server
- Security issues that affect connecting clients (crashes, RCE)

Usually you'll get a warning first. Repeat offenses = removed without
notice. Build good ops habits now so you don't get caught out later.

## Notes
- Advertising is one-way-ish: you can flip it back off, but bookmarks
  persist. Changing the public IP / server_url is the only way to "hide"
  once out.
- Being on multiple hubs doesn't increase your grief risk — the SAME
  players see you via different launchers. It just reaches more people.
notes:
## Pre-flip prereq added — 2026-04-26

Add to the pre-flip checklist:
- [ ] CDN publish pipeline verified end-to-end (vs-2f8.11 closed) —
      this is the H3 from vs-2f8.1's split. We don't want the hub flip
      to send cold launcher traffic at a server whose Manifest
      fetch hasn't been validated since the Local-mode cleanup.

H1 (vs-2f8.10) and H2 (vs-2f8.11) both block this; H3 (signoff) is
the act of confirming both closed before flipping.

title: ops: assess + selectively fork ss14 ancillary services (cookbook, map-server, etc.)
description:
## Context
Ancillary SS14 ecosystem services assessed. This bead is the
**decision record**. Per-service work is tracked in child beads.

## Guiding principle (per user direction)

**External upstream lives as git submodules under `external/` in this
repo. Our config lives in `ops/<service>/` alongside. We only edit
code in this monorepo when customization is actually needed; until
then the submodule pins a specific upstream SHA and upstream LICENSE
files stay intact under that directory.**

This pattern:
- Extends the existing RobustToolbox-submodule approach to all third-
  party services
- Pins upstream SHAs (reproducibility + controlled updates)
- Co-locates code (submodule) + config (ops/) in one repo — no
  separate host-level clones to maintain
- Attribution / LICENSE compliance: upstream LICENSE files remain
  inside the submodule directory, automatically satisfying AGPL/MIT
  attribution rules
- Graduation to "monorepo fork" becomes explicit: `git rm` the
  submodule, copy the code into `services/<name>/`, start editing
  freely

## Decision matrix (final)

| Repo | Verdict | Child bead | Path in repo |
|---|---|---|---|
| [arimah/ss14-cookbook](https://github.com/arimah/ss14-cookbook) | submodule + config | vs-1vy | `external/cookbook/` + `ops/cookbook/` |
| [TrixxedHeart/ss14-paper-sim](https://github.com/TrixxedHeart/ss14-paper-sim) | SKIP | — | — |
| [yagwog/RMC14-document-simu](https://github.com/yagwog/RMC14-document-simu) | submodule + config | vs-v69 | `external/document-sim/` + `ops/document-sim/` |
| [space-wizards/SS14.MapServer](https://github.com/space-wizards/SS14.MapServer) | submodule + config | vs-236 | `external/map-server/` + `ops/map-server/` |
| [space-wizards/SS14.MapViewer](https://github.com/space-wizards/SS14.MapViewer) | rewrite in website | (vs-2dr) | `web/src/app/maps/` |
| [space-wizards/wizard-cogs](https://github.com/space-wizards/wizard-cogs) | inspect only | (vs-2l2) | — (port logic, don't vendor) |
| [space-wizards/SS14.Admin](https://github.com/space-wizards/SS14.Admin) | submodule + config | vs-35d | `external/admin/` + `ops/admin/` |
| [space-wizards/Robust.Cdn](https://github.com/space-wizards/Robust.Cdn) | defer | vs-3mv | (future: `external/cdn/` + `ops/cdn/`) |

## Repo layout (final)
```
vacation-station-14/
├── Content.{Server,Client,Shared}/     game code — owned, AGPL/MIT mix
├── RobustToolbox/                      submodule (engine, existing)
├── external/                           NEW — upstream submodules we deploy but don't edit
│   ├── cookbook/                       → arimah/ss14-cookbook
│   ├── map-server/                     → space-wizards/SS14.MapServer
│   ├── admin/                          → space-wizards/SS14.Admin
│   └── document-sim/                   → yagwog/RMC14-document-simu
├── web/                                Next.js site (vs-2dr), embeds MapViewer
├── services/                           our own code (edited)
│   └── discord-bot/                    (vs-2l2)
├── ops/                                configs + deploy artifacts per service
│   ├── observability/                  existing
│   ├── watchdog/                       existing
│   ├── postgres/                       existing
│   ├── cookbook/                       sources.yml, privacy.html, Caddy block, build script
│   ├── map-server/                     docker-compose, appsettings, GH App private-key location
│   ├── admin/                          docker-compose, appsettings, OAuth env file
│   └── document-sim/                   deploy script, Caddy block
└── docs/
    └── upstream-sync.md                tracks every submodule URL + pinned SHA
```

## Submodule lifecycle
### Adding
```bash
git submodule add https://github.com/<upstream>/<repo> external/<name>
git config -f .gitmodules submodule.external/<name>.branch <main|master>
git config -f .gitmodules submodule.external/<name>.ignore dirty
git add .gitmodules
git commit -m ":heavy_plus_sign: add external/<name> submodule pinning <sha>"
```

`ignore = dirty` matches RobustToolbox's config — prevents the
submodule's working-tree dirty-ness from leaking into our status.

### Updating (pin bump)
```bash
cd external/<name>
git fetch origin
git checkout <target-sha>
cd -
git add external/<name>
git commit -m ":arrow_up: bump external/<name> to <sha>"
```

### Promoting to in-tree fork (when we actually need to edit code)
```bash
# 1. Move code out of submodule tracking
git submodule deinit external/<name>
git rm external/<name>
rm -rf .git/modules/external/<name>

# 2. Copy the code into monorepo
git clone https://github.com/<upstream>/<repo> /tmp/<name>-work
cp -r /tmp/<name>-work/ services/<name>/  # or wherever it belongs
rm -rf services/<name>/.git

# 3. Commit as our own
git add services/<name>/
git commit -m ":arrow_up_small: promote external/<name> into services/<name> for <reason>"

# 4. Update docs/upstream-sync.md to reflect the new relationship
```

This is a deliberate, documented process. Don't promote casually —
every promotion adds a repo we have to keep in sync.

## `docs/upstream-sync.md` table shape
| Service | Upstream | Our mode | Path | Pinned SHA | Last sync |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Game | DeltaV-Station/Delta-v | hard-fork | repo root | n/a (merge) | |
| Engine | space-wizards/RobustToolbox | submodule | `RobustToolbox/` | (from gitlink) | |
| Cookbook | arimah/ss14-cookbook | submodule | `external/cookbook/` | | |
| MapServer | space-wizards/SS14.MapServer | submodule | `external/map-server/` | | |
| Admin | space-wizards/SS14.Admin | submodule | `external/admin/` | | |
| Doc-sim | yagwog/RMC14-document-simu | submodule | `external/document-sim/` | | |
| CDN | space-wizards/Robust.Cdn | deferred | n/a | n/a | n/a |

## `/upstream-sync` skill updates
Extend the skill to cover:
1. Periodic submodule updates (pin bumps)
2. Submodule conflict resolution during Delta-V merges
3. Promotion flow (external → services/)
4. License-compliance reminder on each bump

## Global acceptance criteria
- [x] Per-service verdict recorded with upstream URL
- [ ] `external/` directory created with its submodules
- [ ] `docs/upstream-sync.md` committed with all rows
- [ ] `/upstream-sync` skill updated for submodule workflows
- [ ] vs-3tq license audit passes on initial import

## License audit
Tracked in **vs-3tq** — each submodule must have its LICENSE file
retained at the path `external/<name>/LICENSE(.txt)` to satisfy MIT
attribution + AGPL notice retention. This is automatic with the
submodule approach since we're not modifying the upstream tree.
close_reason: Decision record complete. Per-service verdict matrix documented in description; implementation tracked via vs-1vy (cookbook), vs-236 (mapserver), vs-35d (admin), vs-v69 (doc-sim), vs-3mv (cdn-deferred), all parented under vs-2f8 (ops hardening).

title: ops: add services-flake dev stack (postgres + observability)
description:
## Context
Production bring-up of postgres + prometheus + loki + grafana is handled by the ops scripts + docker-compose we shipped (vs-3ty/vs-h3u/vs-2p3). That path is correct for the Ubuntu host. For local dev we want a zero-sudo, ephemeral equivalent so contributors can validate config changes without touching docker or a real host.

services-flake (https://community.flake.parts/services-flake) is a flake-parts module set that wraps process-compose to run a stack of services as user processes with data under a project-local dir.

Goal: `nix run .#dev-services` boots postgres + prometheus + loki + grafana on localhost against the SAME configs we committed in `ops/`, with data in `.data/` (gitignored).

## Dependencies
- vs-2ti (ops validation tools in dev shell) — not strictly blocking, but land that first so `promtool` etc. are available to validate configs the dev stack loads.

## Task
Extend `flake.nix` to add a services-flake output that composes:
- `services.postgres.pg1` — port 5432, database `vacation_station`, user `vs14`, password `dev-only-insecure` (literal — this is dev-only, document that)
- `services.prometheus.prom1` — config from `ops/observability/prometheus.yml` (or a dev-overlay that points the scrape target at the dev SS14 server port on localhost)
- `services.loki.loki1` — config from `ops/observability/loki-config.yml` (or dev-overlay as needed)
- `services.grafana.graf1` — admin password `admin` (dev only), provisioning dir pointing at `ops/observability/grafana/provisioning`, dashboards dir at `ops/observability/grafana/dashboards`

## Scope
1. **`flake.nix` inputs**: add `services-flake` (from `github:juspay/services-flake`) and `process-compose-flake` (`github:platonic-systems/process-compose-flake`).
2. **`flake.nix` outputs**: switch from `flake-utils.lib.eachDefaultSystem` to `flake-parts.lib.mkFlake` (services-flake requires flake-parts). Preserve the existing `devShells.default = import ./shell.nix { inherit pkgs; }` output — don't break the dev shell that's already working.
3. **New flake output**: `packages.<system>.dev-services` (or `apps.<system>.dev-services`) — the process-compose entrypoint.
4. **Service configs**:
   - Postgres: `initialDatabases = [{ name = "vacation_station"; }]` to match prod schema
   - Prometheus: load our committed `ops/observability/prometheus.yml`. If the `scrape_configs` target `host.docker.internal:44880` needs a dev override (docker-specific hostname won't resolve in dev), put a small nix-side overlay that rewrites the target to `localhost:44880`. Document this.
   - Loki: load `ops/observability/loki-config.yml`. If the `path_prefix` needs to be rewritten to a dev-local dir, do it in the nix expression.
   - Grafana: provisioning + dashboards from the committed paths. Datasource URLs point at the dev-stack services.
5. **Data persistence**: all services write state to `.data/{postgres,prometheus,loki,grafana}/` (project-relative). Update root `.gitignore` to ignore `.data/`.
6. **Docs**: add a "Dev Stack" subsection to `docs/DEVELOPMENT.md` (create if absent) covering:
   - `nix run .#dev-services` to start
   - How to view logs (process-compose TUI)
   - How to reset (`rm -rf .data/`)
   - Credentials (dev-only literals; never reuse for prod)
   - Relationship to production (same configs, same schema, different storage)
   - SS14 connection: point game server's `config.toml` `[database]` at `localhost:5432` user `vs14` pw `dev-only-insecure`; `[metrics]` and `[loki]` already point at localhost.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `nix flake check` passes (or at minimum: `nix-instantiate --parse flake.nix` succeeds and `nix flake show` lists the new output)
- [ ] `nix run .#dev-services --help` (or equivalent) resolves — you don't need to actually boot the stack in the worktree, just prove the expression evaluates
- [ ] Existing `devShells.default` still evaluates (preserve `nix develop` behavior)
- [ ] `.data/` gitignored; no committed state files
- [ ] Dev-only credentials clearly commented as such in flake.nix and docs
- [ ] docs/DEVELOPMENT.md section documents bring-up, reset, credentials, schema-parity claim, and point back to vs-3ty/vs-2p3 for prod
- [ ] Single commit, `Bead: vs-1bb` trailer, gitmoji `:sparkles:`

## Out of scope
- Do NOT modify the production setup scripts or docker-compose
- Do NOT add SS14.Watchdog as a services-flake service (it's a single supervisor binary, not a service we'd want in dev alongside the stack — contributors run SS14 directly via `dotnet run` in dev)
- Do NOT attempt to actually boot the stack inside the worktree (process-compose wants a TTY and the services want ports; just prove the expression evaluates)

## Environment note
Prepend `eval "$(direnv export bash)" 2>/dev/null;` to nix commands so the flake toolchain is active. See CLAUDE.md "Nix env in worktree subagents".

## References to consult
- services-flake quickstart: https://community.flake.parts/services-flake
- Available services: https://community.flake.parts/services-flake/services
- flake-parts: https://flake.parts

## Commit
Example message:
```
:sparkles: ops: nix services-flake dev stack for postgres + observability

- flake.nix: add services-flake + process-compose-flake inputs, migrate to flake-parts
- packages.<system>.dev-services: postgres + prometheus + loki + grafana,
  data in ./.data/ (gitignored), binds to localhost, zero sudo required
- Services read the same configs committed in ops/ (with small dev overlays
  for host.docker.internal -> localhost and data paths)
- docs/DEVELOPMENT.md: Dev Stack section (bring-up, reset, credentials,
  schema parity with prod, how to wire a dev SS14 instance against it)
- devShells.default preserved unchanged
- .gitignore: .data/

Dev-only credentials embedded (documented as such). Production path is
unchanged (vs-3ty postgres + vs-2p3 docker-compose stack remain canonical).

Bead: vs-1bb
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>
```

## Context

```
TypeError: o.values(...).filter is not a function
    at _ (/home/ubuntu/vacation-station-14/external/cookbook/bin/recipe-gen.js:1:7534)
```

The earlier pipeline stages succeed (schema generation parses 213
stacks, 281 construction graphs, 151 food sequence elements, 313
