likely expects a data shape one of VS14's Resources/ YAMLs has
diverged from.

## Triage
1. Un-minify `recipe-gen.js` or pull from upstream source (`arimah/
   ss14-cookbook`) to find the call site.
2. Identify which data structure is being traversed (likely `recipes`
   or `microwaveMealRecipes` given the context).
3. Compare VS14's matching prototype YAMLs against what the code
   expects — probably a missing/renamed field from upstream SS14's
   recent schema evolution.
4. Either patch `ops/cookbook/rewrites_vacation.yml` to normalize
   the data, or open an upstream PR against `arimah/ss14-cookbook`.

## Status
- Build pipeline works end-to-end through schema gen; breaks at
  recipe gen.
- `/recipes/` on prod shows a "coming soon" stub.
- Not blocking anything else; purely gate on real recipe output.

## Parent
vs-1vy (cookbook deploy)
notes: Resolved 2026-04-13: root cause was Node.js 20 lacking Iterator Helpers (Map.values().filter is ES2024). Upgraded host to node 22.22.2 via nodesource; cookbook builds clean. Live at https://ss14.zig.computer/recipes/ (796K of generated content).

title: skill: /services — dev (nix services-flake) vs prod (systemd+docker) handbook
description:
## Context
We now have TWO parallel stack realities, and the lines are blurring in
conversations:

1. **Dev (nix services-flake)**: `nix run .#dev-services` boots
   postgres / prometheus / loki / grafana locally with state in
   `./.data/` (gitignored). Zero sudo. Insecure dev-only credentials
   literal in flake.nix. Data ephemeral by design — `rm -rf .data/` to
   reset.

2. **Prod (systemd + docker-compose)**: live on zig-computer right now.
   Postgres via apt + systemd. Watchdog / SS14.Server under
   ss14-watchdog.service. Observability via docker-compose in
   ops/observability/. Real credentials, persistent data in
   /var/lib/, /opt/, docker volumes. Reset = destructive surgery.

Each stack has conventions for bring-up, inspection, reset, and debugging
that are NOT interchangeable. Running dev commands against prod is
catastrophic; running prod commands against dev is usually pointless.
The existing `/nix` skill covers dev; prod is spread across docs/OPERATIONS.md
and tribal memory. Need a handbook.

## Task
Create `.claude/skills/services/SKILL.md`. Contents:

### 1. The two stacks — side-by-side table
Mirror what exists where: each service's dev location + prod location.
Example shape:

| Service | Dev | Prod |
|---|---|---|
| Postgres | services-flake `postgres.pg1`, `.data/postgres/` | apt `postgresql-17`, `/var/lib/postgresql/17/main/`, systemd |
| Prometheus | services-flake `prometheus.prom1` | docker-compose `prom/prometheus:v2.54.1` |
| Loki | services-flake `loki.loki1` | docker-compose `grafana/loki:3.2.1` |
| Grafana | services-flake `grafana.graf1` (:3200) | docker-compose `grafana/grafana:11.3.0` (:3200) |
| Watchdog | N/A (don't run in dev) | systemd `ss14-watchdog.service` |
| SS14 server | `dotnet run` directly | child of watchdog |

### 2. When to use which (decision tree)
| Goal | Stack | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Validate a `prometheus.yml` change | dev | ephemeral, fast reset, can't break prod |
| Test a DB migration | dev | same schema, guest-ignorable creds |
| Investigate a live bug | prod logs | dev reproduction rarely matches real traffic |
| Write a Grafana dashboard | dev first, copy to prod | dev is your scratchpad |
| Reset everything | see reset procedures |   |
| Test Discord webhook config | prod with a scratch channel | real webhook mechanics |

### 3. Bring-up procedures
**Dev** (full sequence):
```bash
eval "$(direnv export bash)"  # if not already
rm -rf .data                  # fresh state, optional
nix run .#dev-services
```

**Prod** (commands, not "walk-throughs" — the actual invocations you
repeat when something's been stopped):
```bash
sudo systemctl start postgresql ss14-watchdog ss14-backup.timer
cd /opt/vacation-station/ops/observability && docker compose up -d
```

### 4. Reset procedures
**Dev nuclear** (cheap, do whenever):
```bash
pkill -f process-compose
rm -rf .data
```

**Prod nuclear** (expensive, only when you've decided):
```bash
sudo systemctl stop ss14-watchdog
docker compose -f /opt/vacation-station/ops/observability/docker-compose.yml down
sudo -u postgres dropdb vacation_station
sudo -u postgres createdb -O vs14 vacation_station
sudo rm -rf /opt/ss14-watchdog/instances/vacation-station/data/*
sudo rm -rf /var/backups/vacation-station/*   # ← consider archiving first!
docker volume rm vs14-observability_{prometheus,loki,grafana}-data
# then full bring-up per section 3
```

Also include **surgical resets** for individual services (just reset
Prometheus TSDB, just drop the DB, etc.).

### 5. Inspection (commands that are different between dev + prod)
- Process tree: dev = `process-compose attach`; prod = `systemctl status`,
  `docker compose ps`
- Logs: dev = process-compose TUI; prod = `journalctl --user -u X` /
  `docker compose logs X`
- Config reload: dev = Ctrl+C + re-run; prod = systemctl restart X /
  docker compose restart X (doesn't re-evaluate YAML unless recreated)
- Port checks: `ss -tln` works for both; the ports are (mostly) identical
  by design

### 6. Secrets handling — different rules
- Dev: literal in flake.nix, documented as dev-only
- Prod: generated on first install (postgres password, watchdog
  ApiToken, grafana admin). Captured in password manager once. Live
  only in `/etc/vacation-station/*.env` (gitignored) or inline in
  `/opt/.../config.toml`, `/opt/.../appsettings.yml` — NEVER in the
  repo

### 7. Gotchas we've hit
- Dev postgres data `/opt/vacation-station/.data/postgres` vs prod
  postgres data `/var/lib/postgresql/17/main` — utterly different;
  don't let scripts confuse them
- Dev Grafana at :3200, prod Grafana at :3200 — SAME PORT → they
  CAN'T run simultaneously on the same host. This is a feature.
- Config file paths: repo-committed templates end in `.example`;
  populated runtime versions are in `/opt/ss14-watchdog/instances/...`
  or `ops/observability/secrets/...`. Don't edit the `.example`
  expecting changes to take effect; it only propagates on fresh
  deploy.

### 8. Quick reference card
One-screen summary of the most-used commands, organized by verb (start,
stop, reset, log, exec into shell, check status).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `.claude/skills/services/SKILL.md` exists, follows the skill
      format (frontmatter with name/description/type)
- [ ] All 8 sections above are populated with real commands (copy-pasted
      from the actual host)
- [ ] Dev nuclear reset tested by running it; resulting fresh boot
      verified
- [ ] Prod nuclear reset procedures reviewed by a second person before
      ever executing (NEVER run this bead's prod reset as a test — it's
      destructive)
- [ ] Cross-link from `/nix` skill + `docs/OPERATIONS.md` pointing to
      this skill

## Out of scope
- Ops SLOs / incident runbooks — separate skill (once we have real
  production incidents to draw from)
- Cost monitoring (you'd want this once the VPS bill becomes a factor)

## Notes
- This skill should feel like an operator's cheat sheet, not a
  walkthrough. Assume the reader already understands the concepts;
  they need the commands fast.
notes: Post-Flavor-A: /services skill content is fork-agnostic. Dev stack (services-flake) already SS14-aware; prod stack ops are engine-level. No rewrite needed — the skill covers both dev and prod patterns that survive the reset unchanged.

title: ops: render SS14 guidebook to static HTML at /guidebook/
description:
## Context

SS14's Guidebook is an in-game knowledge base: Content.Client.Guidebook
renders markdown content from prototype definitions at
`Resources/Prototypes/Guidebook/*.yml`. Players press F1 or use the
in-game button to browse it. It covers game mechanics (how chemistry
works, airlock cycling, antag roles, etc.).

We already expose /recipes (cookbook), /maps (render index), /writer
(document-simu). /guidebook would complete the "reference material
accessible outside the game" trio.

## Scope

Following the same pattern as ops/cookbook/ and ops/map-render/:

1. `ops/guidebook/build.sh` — parse Resources/Prototypes/Guidebook/*.yml,
   extract embedded markdown content, render to HTML. Probably a
   dotnet tool or a python script walking the YAMLs.
2. Resolve SS14-specific markdown extensions:
   - `{texture:<sprite>}` — embed sprite previews
   - `{prototype:<id>}` — link to prototype pages (entities, reactions)
   - `{guidebook:<page>}` — inter-page links
3. Generate a static site with a navigation sidebar + per-page content
4. nginx location `/guidebook/` → alias `/var/www/vs14-guidebook/`
5. Systemd timer: daily rebuild (fast since no dotnet build required)
6. Update landing page (web/placeholder/index.html) with a
   Guidebook link

## Research questions

- Does SS14 expose a `Content.Guidebook.Renderer` or similar? If yes,
  use it (preserves all the in-game rendering behavior). If no, write
  a minimal markdown-to-HTML parser that handles the SS14 extension
  syntax.
- Do any existing forks serve their guidebook to the web? Check Wizden
  / Frontier / HardLight docs sites.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `/guidebook/` serves a navigable HTML version of VS14's
      in-game Guidebook
- [ ] Links between guidebook pages work
- [ ] Sprite previews render (even if lower-quality than the in-game version)
- [ ] Daily rebuild via systemd timer (pattern match cookbook)
- [ ] Landing page links to /guidebook/

## Parent
vs-z7v (community launch readiness)

## Blocks
None (can land anytime; low priority)

title: human: run vs-h3u watchdog setup on host
description:
## Context
vs-h3u shipped setup.watchdog.sh, systemd unit, appsettings.yml.example, instance-bootstrap.sh, and extended config.toml.example + docs/OPERATIONS.md. None of it has run on the host.

## Dependencies
- vs-y6o (postgres host setup) complete — watchdog unit has `After=postgresql.service`

## Task — run on the target host
1. `sudo ./setup.watchdog.sh` (optionally `WATCHDOG_REF=<tag-or-sha> sudo -E ./setup.watchdog.sh` to pin upstream).
   - Creates system user `ss14:ss14`
   - Publishes SS14.Watchdog to `/opt/ss14-watchdog/`
   - Installs `ss14-watchdog.service`, enables (not starts)
   - Generates ApiToken into a fresh `appsettings.yml` (only if absent)
2. Capture the generated ApiToken from `/opt/ss14-watchdog/appsettings.yml`. Store in password manager under "Vacation Station / watchdog / vacation-station ApiToken". Never commit.
3. `sudo ./ops/watchdog/instance-bootstrap.sh` — sets up `/opt/ss14-watchdog/instances/vacation-station/` layout and seeds `config.toml` from the template.
4. Edit `/opt/ss14-watchdog/instances/vacation-station/config.toml`: fill in postgres password from password manager; adjust hub/auth/status tags as desired.
5. Drop a Robust.Server build into `/opt/ss14-watchdog/instances/vacation-station/binaries/` (Local UpdateType needs this for first launch). Until we publish builds, a `dotnet publish` of our content + engine works.
6. Start the service: `sudo systemctl start ss14-watchdog`.
7. Verify:
   - `systemctl is-active ss14-watchdog` → active
   - `pstree -p $(pgrep -f SS14.Watchdog)` → shows `Robust.Server` child
   - `curl -sS http://localhost:5000/instances/vacation-station/ping` responds (exact path per watchdog version)
   - API auth: `curl -u vacation-station:$TOKEN -X POST http://localhost:5000/instances/vacation-station/restart` succeeds
   - Crash recovery: `sudo pkill -f Robust.Server`; confirm watchdog respawns it within TimeoutSeconds (default 60)
8. Firewall:
   - Confirm port 5000 NOT public (`ss -tln | grep :5000` shows 127.0.0.1 only; cloud firewall closed)
   - Confirm UDP 1212 + TCP 1212 open inbound per docs/NETWORKING.md (game server status + main port)

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `systemctl is-active ss14-watchdog` → active
- [ ] Game server running as child of watchdog (pstree)
- [ ] ApiToken stored in password manager
- [ ] API ping + auth'd restart both succeed from localhost
- [ ] Crash recovery verified (kill Robust.Server, watchdog respawns)
- [ ] Port 5000 localhost-only; 1212 open per networking doc
- [ ] Record completion + timestamp in this bead before closing

## Notes
- Loki sink in appsettings.yml is intentionally commented out (waits on vs-2p3). Don't enable yet.
- UpdateType remains `Local` until we have a Manifest CDN. Don't change without planning an update pipeline.
- Report any divergence from setup.watchdog.sh so we can PR fixes back.

title: skill: /vibe-maintainer — maintainer playbook for the agent-era OSS norms
description:
## Context
Maintaining a public open-source project in 2026+ has different norms
than five years ago. Relevant article:
https://steve-yegge.medium.com/vibe-maintainer-a2273a841040

The specific tools and agent names in that article (Gas Town, Mayor,
etc.) are NOT what we're adopting. What we ARE adopting are the
emerging **norms** for AI-assisted OSS maintenance:

1. Expect that most incoming PRs will be AI-assisted. Plan for it
   rather than trying to ban it.
2. "Request changes, go fix your code" is a LAST resort, not a
   default. It starves contributors and they go fork you.
3. Instead, absorb the good parts of each PR, fix whatever else,
   and merge with **attribution preserved**.
4. Triage + review can be agent-assisted; the maintainer spends
   human judgment on the ambiguous subset (often the top 10%).
5. Rejection is serious. Every rejection raises the odds of a
   downstream fork. Reject when you mean it.
6. Solo maintainership + AI is a viable shape for a popular project
   at 2026 tooling levels. Don't pretend you have a review team
   you don't have.

VS14 is tiny today. If it grows, these norms become load-bearing.
Better to encode the pattern now while the board is small.

## Task
Create `.claude/skills/vibe-maintainer/SKILL.md` documenting:

### 1. Philosophy
- Default posture: absorb good from every PR, reject only as a
  principled last resort
- Preserve contributor attribution (git author, Co-Authored-By,
  changelog entry) when we fix-merge
- Optimize for community throughput, not per-PR perfection
- Solo maintainership with AI assistance is the assumption

### 2. Triage categories for incoming PRs
At first read, an agent bins each PR into one of:
- **Easy win**: targeted fix, doc update, dep bump, banned-author
  close, clearly-right contribution
- **Fix-merge candidate**: a small fix away from being an easy win
- **Needs deeper look**: ambiguous in substance or scope

### 3. Decision tree outcomes (10)
When reviewing a needs-deeper-look PR, the recommendation is one of:
1. Easy win (reclassify)
2. Merge (clean; ready)
3. Merge + follow-up (merge now, minor fixup in a subsequent commit)
4. Fix-merge (we pull locally, resolve issues, merge with
   attribution preserved)
5. Cherry-pick (take N of M items; discard rest politely)
6. Split-merge (decompose multi-concern PR; commit separately with
   attribution)
7. Redesign (problem worth solving; their design is wrong; we solve
   it our way; close PR with explanation)
8. Retire (obsolete / superseded; thank + close)
9. Reject (doesn't pay tech-debt weight; polite decline)
10. Request changes (LAST RESORT — documented as a concession to
    cases where contributor preference matters)

### 4. Hygiene rules for VS14 contributors
- Cross-fork pollution: keep `_VS/` separate from `_DV/`, `_NF/`, etc.
- Annotation: `// VS` / `// DV` / `// NF` for modifications to
  upstream-owned files
- No drafts (auto-closed)
- One concern per PR (prefer split-merge if violated)
- Rebase before submission
- Minimal changes — no gratuitous renames or reformats
- Include SS14 `:cl:` changelog block for player-facing changes
- Reference a bead ID for non-trivial changes

### 5. Fix-merge mechanics
When we fix a contributor's PR locally instead of sending it back:
- `git fetch origin pull/<N>/head:pr-<N>`
- `git checkout pr-<N>`
- Apply fixes — prefer small surgical changes
- `git rebase main`
- When committing fixes: `git commit --author="Original Author <email>"`
  OR add `Co-Authored-By:` trailer
- Merge via PR or direct push; close the original PR with a
  thank-you + summary of what we did
- Changelog entry credits original author (SS14 `:cl: OriginalName`)

### 6. Attribution discipline
- git author preserved on cherry-picked commits
- `Co-Authored-By:` trailer when we did conflict resolution
- `:cl:` block names the original author even when we fix-merged
- Commit subject includes `(from #<pr-number>)` reference for
  external-PR-origin commits

### 7. Security review for AI-generated contributions
Quick checklist the agent runs on suspicious PRs:
- Any new secrets / tokens / credentials in the diff?
- Any new network endpoints, especially outbound?
- Any new dependencies added? Pinned to specific versions?
- Any auth / identity / admin-path changes?
- Any base64-encoded blobs without clear purpose?

If any hit: escalate to human before merging.

### 8. When to escalate to human
- Substantial architectural changes
- Anything matching the security checklist
- Controversial design calls (PR comments disagree with us)
- Unknown contributor with sweeping changes
- Anything that touches `_DV/` or `_NF/` in a way that conflicts
  with upstream sync expectations

### 9. Cross-references
- Pairs with `/commit` (for our own commits)
- Pairs with `/orchestrator` (agent roles for review + fix-merge)
- Pairs with `/review` (deeper bead-level review)
- Paired bead: vs-2sr (CONTRIBUTING.md) — contributors see this
  skill reflected in our documented hygiene
- Paired bead: vs-f0l (scheduled PR triage workflow) — CI-side
  automation for the "easy win" half of the decision tree

## Acceptance
- [ ] `.claude/skills/vibe-maintainer/SKILL.md` exists
- [ ] All 9 sections above populated with concrete examples
- [ ] Attribution/fix-merge procedures have copy-pasteable commands
- [ ] Cross-links to CONTRIBUTING.md and related skills
- [ ] The skill reads as principles + procedures, not tool-specific
      (no Gas Town branding)

## Dependencies
- Blocks on vs-ddu.2 (post-Flavor-A base state before this skill's
  procedures are codified)

## Not in scope
- Full multi-agent orchestration frameworks (Mayor/polecats/etc)
  — our scale doesn't justify it; our existing /orchestrator is
  enough
- Trust-ranking systems / contributor rep scores
- Automated fix-merge without human in loop (too risky at our scale)
notes:
## Framing note (per user direction)

This skill is NOT about adopting any specific tool or orchestration
framework from external references. It's about acknowledging that the
maintainer / contributor / user dynamics have all shifted in the
agent era, and codifying how WE operate under the new normal.

The shifts:
- **Maintainer**: one human + AI assistance; no volunteer review team
- **Contributor**: AI-assisted humans (or AI agents); higher velocity;
  submission effort is low so expectation is higher
- **User**: expects fast response, low friction, and will fork if we
  drag; every popular project is a credible fork target now

The skill captures: a clear decision tree for what to do with
incoming PRs, attribution discipline when we fix-merge, hygiene rules
for contributors, and escalation criteria for human-only judgment
calls. Reference article (Yegge's "Vibe Maintainer") is useful
background, NOT a methodology to copy.

title: TEST: epic type smoke test
ops: cherry-pick + curate GitHub Actions from upstream forks (agent-supporting)
description:
## Context
After Flavor A Phase 1 lands, our `.github/workflows/` contains
pure upstream SS14's 24 workflows (we documented the drift in
vs-345 — Delta-V added stale.yml, SS14 has labeler-stable/staging +
publish-testing Delta-V didn't). Now we re-examine every workflow
under the vibe-maintainer lens and curate deliberately rather than
inheriting.

## Workflow audit matrix (post-Flavor-A)

Every workflow falls into one of these categories. DECISION required
per workflow.

### Quality gates (KEEP — essential regardless of community size)
| Workflow | Purpose | Decision |
|---|---|---|
| `yaml-linter.yml` | Prototype YAML validation | **KEEP** — invaluable for content authors (us included) |
| `check-crlf.yml` | Line-ending sanity | **KEEP** — cheap, catches Windows cross-editor issues |
| `rsi-diff.yml` | Visual sprite-diff in PR comments | **KEEP** — huge win for agent + human review of visual changes |
| `validate-rsis.yml` | RSI metadata integrity | **KEEP** |
| `validate-rgas.yml` | RGA schema validation | **KEEP** |
| `validate_mapfiles.yml` | Map file schema | **KEEP** |
| `build-test-debug.yml` | Compile + unit tests | **KEEP** — the ground-truth quality gate |
| `test-packaging.yml` | Ensure release packaging succeeds | **KEEP** — vs-ddu.4 learnings |
| `no-submodule-update.yml` | Block accidental submodule bumps | **KEEP** — our pre-commit hook peer |
| `build-map-renderer.yml` | Map preview generation | **KEEP** — supports /maps route in website |

### Publishing (KEEP — we distribute builds)
| Workflow | Purpose | Decision |
|---|---|---|
| `publish.yml` | Production release artifact | **KEEP** — needed if we stand up Robust.Cdn (vs-3mv) |
| `publish-testing.yml` | Testing / beta builds | **KEEP** — staging lane for cherry-picks |

### Community gates (EVALUATE carefully — solo-maintainer reality)
| Workflow | Purpose | Decision |
|---|---|---|
| `labeler-pr.yml` | Auto-apply type labels | **KEEP** — helpful for /vibe-maintainer sheriff |
| `labeler-size.yml` | S/M/L size labels | **KEEP** — essential for sheriff triage |
| `labeler-conflict.yml` | Merge-conflict detection | **KEEP** — high signal for fix-merge path |
| `labeler-needsreview.yml` | Mark needs-review state | **KEEP** |
| `labeler-untriaged.yml` | Default state label | **KEEP** |
| `labeler-stable.yml` | Publication channel tag | **DEFER** — relevant if we do channeled releases |
| `labeler-staging.yml` | Publication channel tag | **DEFER** |
| `labeler-review.yml` | Approved-label bot | **DISABLE** — requires LABELER_PAT secret; solo maintainer doesn't benefit |
| `close-master-pr.yml` | Auto-close wrong-branch PRs | **KEEP** — cheap cleanup |
| `update-credits.yml` | Contributor list auto-append | **KEEP** — guard to our repo name; light attribution win |

### Documentation (EVALUATE — do we run a docs site?)
| Workflow | Purpose | Decision |
|---|---|---|
| `build-docfx.yml` | Generate + publish DocFX docs | **DISABLE** — no docs site; vs-352 player docs go through website not docfx |

### Infra-coupled (SKIP — not our infrastructure)
| Workflow | Purpose | Decision |
|---|---|---|
| `benchmarks.yml` | Perf bench on centcomm | **DISABLE** — centcomm is Wizden; vs-zyk documented skip |

## Additional workflows to ADD (from sibling forks)

From Frontier's `.github/workflows/`:
- `changelog.yml` / `publish-changelog.yml` — pairs with SS14.Changelog
  webhook (vs-3v4); consider as alternative to the webhook for
  post-merge Changelog.yml updates without running a hosted service.
  Decide after vs-3v4 is deployed.

From Einstein-Engines:
- `prtitlecase.yml` — validates PR title case. Nice-to-have; advisory
  only, not blocking. **ADOPT IF LIGHTWEIGHT**.
- `discord-changelog.yml` — Discord announcement pipeline. Pairs with
  vs-2l2; consider once Discord bot phases are live.

From this work, NET changes post-Flavor-A:
- DISABLE (via `gh api .../disable`): labeler-review, build-docfx, benchmarks
- DEFER (no action): labeler-stable, labeler-staging (re-evaluate if
  we stand up channeled releases)
- ADOPT (cherry-pick / port): prtitlecase (low-risk), maybe changelog.yml
- SS14's all others: KEEP as-is

## Task
1. Execute the decisions in the matrix above, via the vs-345 epic's
   existing per-workflow child beads (vs-j78, vs-12b, vs-39z, vs-367,
   vs-zyk — some may fold in or spawn siblings).
2. For each DISABLE decision: `gh api -X PUT /repos/.../actions/workflows/<id>/disable`
3. For each ADOPT decision: copy workflow file in; test via workflow_dispatch
4. Update `docs/OPERATIONS.md` with a "CI Workflows" section listing
   every active workflow + its purpose + who it notifies

## Acceptance
- [ ] Matrix above is executed — every workflow has a decision applied
- [ ] Agent-supporting additions (prtitlecase if chosen) working
- [ ] docs/OPERATIONS.md "CI Workflows" section complete
- [ ] First post-curation PR runs only the intended workflows
- [ ] vs-345's child beads (vs-j78, vs-12b, vs-39z, vs-367, vs-zyk)
      all closed through this work

## Dependencies
- Blocks on vs-ddu.2 (clear commit resets workflows to SS14's)
- Blocks on vs-1ss (/vibe-maintainer skill — decision framework)

## Out of scope
- Custom benchmarking infrastructure (separate bead if we ever want it)
- Custom docs site (separate bead; vs-352 explores via wiki)
- Canary / staged rollouts (separate bead; tied to Robust.Cdn vs-3mv)

## Notes
- This bead replaces the scattered individual workflow-decision beads
  with a single audit-and-execute pass. The individual beads stay open
  for per-workflow tracking but close as this pass completes them.
notes:
## Framing note
The audit isn't "which workflows to keep from Delta-V vs SS14" — it's
"which workflows make sense for a solo + AI maintainer in 2026+."
Some inherited workflows assumed a multi-person review team with a
shared PAT-bot; those get disabled. Quality gates stay (they protect
everyone regardless of team shape). New workflows get added to emit
agent-readable context the maintainer's review agent needs.

The matrix in the main description categorizes each workflow
accordingly.

title: legal: public-facing TOS, privacy policy, DMCA contact, data retention
description:
## Context
The moment VS14 is public — hub-advertised, collecting player accounts,
retaining logs, running Discord — legal obligations attach. Different
jurisdictions apply based on hosting location (VPS in France per the
51.81.x.x IP block, so French + EU data protection law applies), user
location (GDPR-reach is worldwide for EU residents), and operator
location (you).

Blank/absent legal framing is fine for an invite-only test. For a
public hub launch it's minimally negligent and potentially actively
harmful (liability, DMCA takedowns with no process).

## Task — minimum viable legal framework

### 1. Terms of Service
`docs/community/legal/tos.md` + published at `vacation.<domain>/tos`.
Cover at minimum:
- Acceptance by connecting / using the service
- Age requirement (13+ COPPA, 16+ for EEA per GDPR)
- Acceptable use (cross-reference server rules)
- Account termination rights (bans — we do this; TOS grounds us)
- IP assignment (none — users keep their words; we don't claim their chat)
- Disclaimer of warranty (game is provided as-is)
- Limitation of liability (we're not responsible for damages)
- Change-of-terms procedure
- Governing law (France / where you operate)

### 2. Privacy Policy
`docs/community/legal/privacy.md` + `vacation.<domain>/privacy`.
Required by GDPR, CCPA, and basic decency. Cover:
- What we collect: username (Wizden OAuth'd or guest), IP address
  (logged transiently by watchdog), chat logs, admin actions, Discord
  account if they join, round replays (sensitive — see vs-2l1)
- Why we collect each: moderation, crash debugging, gameplay
- Retention period for each type: chat logs 30d, admin actions
  indefinite (required for ban appeals), replays variable (tie to
  vs-2l1 retention), Discord data indefinite while member
- Third parties: Wizards Den (identity/auth), Discord (their platform's
  TOS applies), VPS host (incidental, DPA in place)
- User rights: access, export, deletion (how to request)
- Data controller contact (email)

### 3. DMCA / Takedown process
`docs/community/legal/dmca.md` — required if we host user content
(replays, map submissions). Even if we think it's unlikely someone'd
DMCA us, having a process means:
- A named agent to receive notices (email, postal address)
- Procedure for takedown + counter-notice
- Safe-harbor compliance so we're not liable for user infringement

### 4. Data Retention Policy (internal-facing, but publishable)
`docs/community/legal/retention.md`:
- Which data, how long, why, deletion mechanism
- Ban-evasion / permanent-identifier policy
- Backup retention (pg_dumps held 28 days, then gone)
- Log retention (journal 30d, syslog 5w)
- Replay retention (14d raw / 180d metadata — per vs-2l1)
- Incident retention (security events held 1y)

### 5. Cookie Policy (if the website uses them)
If vs-2dr uses any analytics cookies, first-party auth cookies for
admin, etc., need a cookie banner + policy.

## Execution
1. Start with templates (Termly, iubenda, or public-domain templates
   from the EFF). Do NOT just copy from another server.
2. Have the templates reviewed BY A LAWYER if we expect meaningful
   player volume or any donations. Free/template legal is a starting
   point, not an endpoint.
3. Publish on website under `/legal/*` routes.
4. Link from website footer + Discord #rules + game MOTD.
5. Name a DPA (data protection officer) contact — likely yourself
   for now.

\#\# Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] TOS published
- [ ] Privacy Policy published with real retention numbers
- [ ] DMCA process documented with named agent
- [ ] Data retention policy documented + matches actual infra
      retention (backup cron, journald caps, replay retention)
- [ ] Legal footer linked from website, Discord, game MOTD
- [ ] Optional: lawyer review commissioned if scope justifies

## Dependencies
- vs-2dr (website serves /legal pages)
- vs-2l1 (replay retention policy feeds data retention)
- All infra retention decisions (we should be honest about what we
  actually keep and for how long)

## Out of scope
- Full incorporation / business entity setup (if VS14 becomes a real
  non-profit or company later, separate bead)
- EULA for the game engine (that's RobustToolbox's responsibility)

## Notes
- Boring but necessary. Don't skip.
- GDPR fines are per-record for noncompliance. Don't collect what you
  don't need.
- Transparency = trust. Under-promise retention (say 30d, actually
  keep 14d) — hard to get in trouble for deleting TOO much.
notes:
## 2026-05-02 — drafting started; scope clarified

The original blocks-on vs-2dr dep was tied to "publish at
vacation.<domain>/tos" routes. Removed because:

- The drafting work (text content of TOS / privacy / retention) is
  independent of website infrastructure
- Drafted docs live at docs/community/legal/*.md and are
  immediately accessible via the public GitHub repo
- /tos / /privacy / /retention URL routing is a downstream task
  that rides with vs-2dr (website bootstrap)

Maintainer-pinned scoping decisions for the drafts (2026-05-02):
- Governing law: California
- Data controller contact: legal@zig.computer
- Age floor: 16+ globally (no 13+/EEA split; rules.md updated
  this session in d89d5ac706)
- Cookies: only essential — no separate cookie policy needed
- DMCA: skip registered-agent listing per § 512; include
  "Reporting copyright concerns" paragraph in TOS pointing at
  legal@zig.computer instead

Drafts in flight: TOS (under maintainer review now); privacy +
retention drafted next once TOS is approved.

title: ops: deploy vanilla ss14-cookbook configured for VS14
description:
## Context
Parent: **vs-19h** (decision matrix + submodule convention).

Use arimah/ss14-cookbook as-is (no fork) via submodule at
`external/cookbook/`. VS14-specific config lives in `ops/cookbook/`.
Build on deploy; serve static output via Caddy.

## Task
1. Add submodule:
   ```
   git submodule add https://github.com/arimah/ss14-cookbook external/cookbook
   git config -f .gitmodules submodule.external/cookbook.branch main
   git config -f .gitmodules submodule.external/cookbook.ignore dirty
   git add .gitmodules
   git commit -m ":heavy_plus_sign: add external/cookbook submodule"
   ```
2. Add `ops/cookbook/`:
   - `sources.yml` — points at VS14's Resources/ (via a sibling
     read-only clone of VS14 maintained on the host, since cookbook
     needs yaml+png files, not nix-built output). Path variable.
   - `privacy.html` — our privacy notice (derives from vs-1ux).
   - `rewrites_vacation.yml` — per-VS14 recipe rewrites (empty at
     first; populate when we spot recipes that don't render).
   - `build.sh` — wraps `npm ci && npm run build && npm run gen:recipes`,
     rsync's `external/cookbook/public/` to the served dir (e.g.
     `/var/www/cookbook.vacation.<domain>/`).
   - `Caddyfile.block` — snippet for `cookbook.vacation.<domain>`.
   - `vs14-cookbook-build.service` + `.timer` — daily rebuild
     triggered systemd unit.
3. Sibling clone: the cookbook needs a separate VS14 checkout to
   parse (it reads Resources/ files directly; shouldn't share with
   our dev tree). Script in `ops/cookbook/` that clones / updates a
   read-only mirror at `/var/lib/vs14-cookbook-source/`.
4. AGPLv3 compliance: the deployed cookbook's footer must include a
   "View Source" link pointing at `github.com/azigler/vacation-station-14`.
   Verify the template either has a footer-customization option or
   do a small post-build patch (belongs under Phase 2 if post-build
   patch required — record as promotion trigger).
5. Optional upstream contribution: PR against arimah's `sources.real.yml`
   listing VS14 so we appear on ss14.recipes.
6. Update `docs/upstream-sync.md` with cookbook row.

## Acceptance
- [ ] `external/cookbook/` submodule at a pinned SHA
- [ ] `ops/cookbook/` configs committed
- [ ] Build + deploy works end-to-end
- [ ] Served at cookbook.vacation.<domain> with HTTPS
- [ ] AGPLv3 source-link visible on deployed site
- [ ] docs/upstream-sync.md updated

## Promotion triggers (move to services/cookbook/)
- We need post-build code edits and can't make them config-driven
- Upstream rejects PRs we want merged
- We need VS14-specific UI panels / theming beyond config

## Dependencies
- vs-2y8 (Caddy)
- vs-1ux (privacy policy text)
- vs-3tq (license audit — AGPL compliance gate)
notes: Post-Flavor-A: cookbook reads Resources/ from our repo clone; post-reset it sees pure SS14 prototypes + our _VS content. Fork-in-sources.yml still works — no config change required.

title: docs: networking guide with caddy and firewall setup
description:
## Context
User is hosting on a headless VPS. Needs documentation for accessing the server
from outside, firewall considerations (ufw), and adding a domain name via Caddy.

## Task
Write docs/NETWORKING.md covering:
- App binding vs firewall (two layers)
- ufw basics and setup
- Cloud provider firewall
- Domain name setup (DNS, config)
- Caddy reverse proxy for HTTPS on status API
- UDP can't be proxied (kept direct)

description:
## Context
Community events (special rounds, dev streams, community game nights,
holiday events) need a scheduling home that's visible everywhere a

title: human: verify vs-13x dashboards load in grafana
description:
## Context
vs-13x shipped two adapted Grafana dashboards (game-servers.json, perf-metrics.json) into ops/observability/grafana/dashboards/ plus docs. Grafana's file provider will pick them up automatically on container start, but nobody has actually confirmed they render correctly against live data.

## Dependencies
- vs-25k (observability stack running) complete — Grafana must be up and datasources green

## Task — verify on the host with a running stack
1. Ensure grafana container has the latest dashboards: `docker compose -f ops/observability/docker-compose.yml restart grafana` (the file provider rescans on boot).
2. In Grafana UI → Dashboards: confirm both appear:
   - "Vacation Station Servers" (uid `vs14-game-servers`)
   - "Vacation Station Perf Metrics" (uid `vs14-perf-metrics`)
3. On **Game Servers**:
   - All panels render without the red "Datasource not found" banner
   - Player-count / round-length / server-list panels populate once SS14 is running
   - Connections panel (Postgres) shows at least 1 row (the grafana session itself counts)
4. On **Perf Metrics**:
   - The `$Server` dropdown populates with `vacation-station` from `label_values(ss14_round_length{job="gameservers"}, server)`
   - Logs panel streams live Loki logs: `{App="Robust.Server",Server="vacation-station"}`
   - Perf panels (tick rate, process metrics) populate
5. Known TODOs to either resolve or backlog:
   - **TPS alert notifier** — upstream references notification UID `N5nihcmMk` that doesn't exist locally. Grafana logs "missing notifier"; alert still fires internally but can't deliver. Either create a local contact point + rebind, or delete the alert rule until alerting scope is formally opened.
   - **Stale `byName` overrides** for wizards_den_eu_west / us_west — harmless no-ops on our single-instance deployment; prune at your leisure via UI edit + export.
   - **Datasource uid fragility** — dashboards bind to datasource NAMES (`Prometheus`, `Loki`, `Postgres`). If someone later adds explicit `uid:` fields to datasources.yml, the dashboards will silently unbind. Mitigation: pin datasource uids to lowercase names in datasources.yml AND rewrite the dashboard JSONs to match.
6. If anything breaks, file a follow-up `fix:` bead referencing vs-13x and the specific panel/UID at fault.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Both dashboards visible under Dashboards in Grafana UI with the pinned UIDs
- [ ] All panels on both dashboards render without datasource errors
- [ ] `$Server` variable on Perf Metrics populates from live Prometheus labels
- [ ] Logs panel on Perf Metrics streams live log lines from the running SS14 server
- [ ] Decision recorded on the TPS alert notifier TODO (local contact point or removed)
- [ ] Record completion + timestamp before closing

## Notes
- A Robust.Server must be actively running for most panels to show data. First-boot empty panels are expected; re-check after a round has started.
- Dashboards are provisioned read-only. To iterate, "Save As..." a copy, then export + replace the committed JSON, then `docker compose restart grafana`.

title: ops: deploy vanilla SS14.MapServer configured for VS14
description:
## Context
Parent: **vs-19h** (decision matrix + submodule convention).

Use space-wizards/SS14.MapServer as-is via submodule at
`external/map-server/`. VS14-specific config in `ops/map-server/`.
One-deployment-per-fork by design (`Git.RepositoryUrl` targets a
single upstream).

## Task
1. Add submodule:
   ```
   git submodule add https://github.com/space-wizards/SS14.MapServer external/map-server
   git config -f .gitmodules submodule.external/map-server.branch master
   git config -f .gitmodules submodule.external/map-server.ignore dirty
   ```
2. `ops/map-server/`:
   - `docker-compose.yml` — `build: context: ../../external/map-server`,
     bind `127.0.0.1:5218`, named volumes for `files` + `build`, sidecar
     postgres container scoped to this service.
   - `appsettings.yaml` — `Git.RepositoryUrl` = our repo,
     `Branch: main`, map file patterns including `_VS`,
     `MapServer DB` connection to the sidecar postgres,
     `CorsOrigins` = our web domain.
   - `.env.example` — `MAPSERVER_POSTGRES_PASSWORD=`, any GH App keys
     (if we decide to register as a GitHub App — optional; without it
     fall back to `RetrieveMapFilesFromDiff: false`).
   - `Caddyfile.block` — `maps.vacation.<domain>` → `127.0.0.1:5218`.
3. Systemd unit `vs14-map-server.service` wrapping compose up/down.
4. GitHub App registration (optional): follow upstream's quickstart
   if we want diff-based rebuilds. Otherwise simpler config.
5. `docs/OPERATIONS.md` section.
6. Update `docs/upstream-sync.md` with map-server row.

## Acceptance
- [ ] `external/map-server/` submodule
- [ ] `ops/map-server/` configs
- [ ] Docker stack builds + boots
- [ ] Renders ≥1 VS14 map
- [ ] Caddy-fronted HTTPS

## Promotion triggers
- Custom UI / theming beyond config
- Bespoke rendering (tile size, parallax, watermark)

## Dependencies
- vs-2y8 (Caddy)

## Disk budget
Rendered maps + build volumes can balloon. Add to disk monitoring.
Start with 20 GB allocation.
notes:
## Scope correction (2026-04-12)

Original bead says "SS14.MapServer"; the actual target for
`/maps/` is **SS14.MapViewer** — the player-facing static web app.
MapServer is a separate backend (webhook-driven map-render service)
that MapViewer can optionally consume.

### Corrected architecture
- `ss14.zig.computer/maps/` → static MapViewer build, served by
  nginx from `/var/www/vs14-maps/`
- Backend (if adopted): SS14.MapServer on loopback, consumed by
  MapViewer's fetch calls; routed through nginx under a
  sub-location if needed
- Alternative backend: `Content.MapRenderer` (upstream SS14 tool)
  to pre-render tiles on a timer — no MapServer required for a
  first pass

### First-pass plan (simpler)
1. Submodule: `external/mapviewer` → space-wizards/SS14.MapViewer
2. `ops/mapviewer/`: build script, config, systemd unit if needed
3. Build output rsync'd to `/var/www/vs14-maps/`
4. `Content.MapRenderer` invocation in a build script produces tile
   images; MapViewer points at them (static mode)
5. Later (separate bead): deploy SS14.MapServer if we want dynamic
   renders on merge

### Current state
- nginx `/maps/` serves `/var/www/vs14-maps/` with a "coming soon"
  stub (HTTP 200)
- Submodule + build pipeline pending

title: human: bring up vs-2p3 observability stack on host
description:
## Context
vs-2p3 shipped docker-compose + prometheus/loki/grafana configs + SS14/watchdog wiring + ops docs. Nothing is running on the host. This bead captures the host-only bring-up.

## Dependencies
- vs-y6o (postgres host setup) complete — Grafana Postgres datasource expects it
- vs-1np (watchdog host setup) complete — Loki receives watchdog + game server logs
- Docker Engine installed on the host (if not yet: `curl -fsSL https://get.docker.com | sh` or per distro)

## Task — run on the target host
1. **Bootstrap secrets** (NONE committed):
   - `mkdir -p ops/observability/secrets`
   - `openssl rand -base64 32 > ops/observability/secrets/grafana_admin_password.txt`
   - `cp ops/observability/.env.example ops/observability/.env`
   - Edit `ops/observability/.env`: set `POSTGRES_PASSWORD=` to the vs14 Postgres password from password manager
   - Confirm both files gitignored (`.gitignore` in ops/observability/ handles this — verify)
2. **Bring up the stack**:
   - `docker compose -f ops/observability/docker-compose.yml up -d`
   - `docker compose -f ops/observability/docker-compose.yml ps` — all three services healthy
3. **Verify endpoints** (all localhost):
   - `curl -sS localhost:9090/api/v1/targets | jq '.data.activeTargets[] | {job: .labels.job, health}'` — `gameservers` target reports `up` once SS14 is running
   - `curl -sS localhost:3100/ready` → `ready`
   - `curl -sS localhost:3000/api/health` → `{"database":"ok"}`
4. **Grafana login**:
   - Browse to `http://localhost:3000` (port-forward via SSH if remote)
   - Login as `admin` with password from `grafana_admin_password.txt`
   - Change admin password on first login (Grafana forces this)
   - Store the final admin password in password manager under "Vacation Station / grafana / admin"
5. **Datasource verification**:
   - Grafana → Connections → Data sources: Prometheus, Loki, PostgreSQL all auto-provisioned, all test-connection green
   - PostgreSQL datasource only works if `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` in `.env` is correct and Postgres `pg_hba.conf` permits host.docker.internal (127.0.0.1 usually fine)
6. **Metric + log sanity checks** (requires SS14 game server running):
   - In Grafana Explore with Prometheus: `robust_player_count{server="vacation-station"}` returns a series
   - In Grafana Explore with Loki: `{App="Robust.Server",Server="vacation-station"}` returns log lines
   - Watchdog logs: `{Server="vacation-station-watchdog"}` or whatever Name you configured
7. **SS14 side wiring**:
   - Confirm `/opt/ss14-watchdog/instances/vacation-station/config.toml` has the `[metrics]` and `[loki]` blocks from config.toml.example
   - Confirm `/opt/ss14-watchdog/appsettings.yml` has the `GrafanaLoki` Serilog sink enabled
   - Restart watchdog to pick up changes: `sudo systemctl restart ss14-watchdog`
8. **Firewall**:
   - `ss -tln | grep -E ':(9090|3100|3000)'` — all three bound to 127.0.0.1 only
   - Public Grafana via Caddy only (see docs/NETWORKING.md snippet)
9. **Caddy** (if external access desired):
   - Add the `grafana.yourdomain.com` block from docs/NETWORKING.md to your Caddyfile
   - `sudo systemctl reload caddy`
   - Verify HTTPS cert issued and proxy works

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `docker compose ps` shows prometheus + loki + grafana healthy
- [ ] `curl localhost:9090/api/v1/targets` shows `gameservers` target `up`
- [ ] `curl localhost:3100/ready` → `ready`
- [ ] Grafana admin password rotated on first login and stored in password manager
- [ ] All three datasources test-green in Grafana UI
- [ ] Prometheus + Loki sample queries return data (once SS14 is running)
- [ ] Ports 9090/3100/3000 localhost-only (confirmed with ss)
- [ ] Caddy HTTPS proxy functional (if external Grafana desired)
- [ ] Record completion timestamp before closing

## Notes
- Dashboards (vs-13x) land separately — this bead is stack bring-up only.
- If Prometheus `gameservers` target shows `down`, check that SS14 `[metrics] host = "localhost"` and the watchdog instance has actually started the game server on port 44880.
- Loki retention is 30d — raise by editing `ops/observability/loki-config.yml` `retention_period` and restarting the loki container.

title: human: run setup.ubuntu.sh --server on prod host
description:
## Context
All the other prod human beads (vs-y6o postgres, vs-1np watchdog, vs-25k observability, vs-205 dashboards) assume the host already has the baseline runtime: .NET 10 SDK + ASP.NET Core 10 runtime, git, python, build tools, firewall tooling. `setup.ubuntu.sh` is the committed script that does that. This bead is the bootstrap step they all depend on.

Nix is the primary DEV path (see docs/DEVELOPMENT.md and /nix skill), but production hosts run system-installed .NET via this script — not nix.

## Dependencies
- None (this is the root of the prod install tree)

## Blocks
- vs-y6o (postgres host setup)
- vs-1np (watchdog host setup) — specifically needs .NET 10 SDK to `dotnet publish` SS14.Watchdog from source
- vs-25k (observability stack bring-up) — docker is typically installed separately but `setup.ubuntu.sh --server` may or may not include it (verify)
- vs-205 (dashboard verification) — transitively via vs-25k

## Task — run on the target host

1. **Fresh-host sanity**: `lsb_release -a` should report Ubuntu 22.04 or 24.04 (what setup.ubuntu.sh targets). If not, confirm parity or switch host.
2. **Clone repo**: `git clone https://github.com/azigler/vacation-station-14.git /opt/vacation-station` (or wherever you want production repo root; this matches the path ops/watchdog/ss14-backup.service assumes).
3. **Run setup.ubuntu.sh**: `cd /opt/vacation-station && sudo ./setup.ubuntu.sh --server`.
   - `--server` flag omits the client-only graphics/audio deps (no X, no OpenGL, no PulseAudio). Keeps the host minimal.
   - If `--server` flag isn't implemented yet in the committed script, check what flags it takes and pick the server-minimal path; if only a single mode exists, run without flag and report what got installed.
   - Script should install: .NET 10 SDK, ASP.NET Core 10 runtime, git, python3, curl, build-essential.
4. **Verify .NET**: `dotnet --version` reports a 10.x SDK; `dotnet --list-runtimes` includes `Microsoft.AspNetCore.App 10.x`.
5. **Verify python**: `python3 --version` ≥ 3.7 (for `RUN_THIS.py`).
6. **Initialize submodule**: `cd /opt/vacation-station && python3 RUN_THIS.py` — pulls RobustToolbox.
7. **Install Docker** (if not already, needed for vs-25k observability stack): `curl -fsSL https://get.docker.com | sudo sh` and `sudo usermod -aG docker $USER` (log out/in or `newgrp docker`). Verify: `docker compose version` → v2.x.
8. **Firewall baseline** (see docs/NETWORKING.md for full detail): `sudo ufw allow OpenSSH`, `sudo ufw enable`. Other per-service ports come from subsequent beads (1212 for SS14, etc.).
9. **Create ops user** (if setup.ubuntu.sh doesn't): `ss14` system user + group referenced by the watchdog systemd unit (vs-h3u script creates it but sanity-check here that `id ss14` works after its install).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Ubuntu 22.04 or 24.04 confirmed
- [ ] `/opt/vacation-station` (or chosen prod path) cloned, main up-to-date
- [ ] `setup.ubuntu.sh` ran cleanly (no error exit)
- [ ] `dotnet --version` ≥ 10.0.x
- [ ] `dotnet --list-runtimes` includes `Microsoft.AspNetCore.App 10.x`
- [ ] `python3 RUN_THIS.py` completes; `RobustToolbox/` is populated
- [ ] `docker compose version` returns ≥ v2.x (install separately if setup.ubuntu.sh doesn't cover it)
- [ ] `ufw status` shows enabled with at least OpenSSH allowed
- [ ] Record completion timestamp + any setup.ubuntu.sh deviations in this bead before closing

## Notes
- setup.ubuntu.sh is *checked in* from upstream Delta-V; it may get updates via upstream-sync. Always pull before running.
- This bead is the **system-install bootstrap**. Contributors doing dev work should use nix/direnv instead (see docs/DEVELOPMENT.md Quick Start (Nix)).
- If anything in `setup.ubuntu.sh` fails or drifts from reality, file a `fix:` bead so we can PR corrections back (especially if deps change in future .NET / Ubuntu releases).
- This bead captures only baseline OS-level setup. Service-specific bring-up (postgres, watchdog, observability, dashboards) are in vs-y6o, vs-1np, vs-25k, vs-205 respectively — run them in that order after this one.

title: bot: port wizard-cogs features (gameserverstatus, poweractions, echo, autoresponder)
description:
## Context
Space Wizards maintains a small library of RedBot (Red-DiscordBot)
cogs at github.com/space-wizards/wizard-cogs for Discord community
automation. Since VS14's bot (vs-2l2) is planned as discord.py (not
RedBot), we don't drop these in; we **port their features** into
our bot's command surface.

## Cogs + port priority

### High-value — implement in Phase 1
- **gameserverstatus**: shows map / player count / round length for
  an SS14 server. Our vs-2l2 bead already has a `/status` slash
  command; this cog's logic is the direct reference implementation
  (polls http://<host>:1212/status + /info; formats an embed).
  Source: `gameserverstatus/gameserverstatus.py`.
- **poweractions**: admin slash commands (`/restart`, `/stop`,
  `/update`) that hit the watchdog admin API (now at
  /watchdog/instances/vacation-station/... after vs-34m). Delivers
  "poke the server from Discord" capability that AHELP over Discord
  enables. Source: `poweractions/poweractions.py`. MUST be gated
  by @Admin role.

### Medium-value — implement in Phase 2
- **echo**: `/echo <message>` and edit-echo, admin-only. Useful for
  announcements without revealing personal Discord account.
  Source: `echo/echo.py` (~20 lines).

### Low-value — optional / flavor
- **autoresponder**: trigger phrases (WYSI, NANOTRASHEN BLOCK GAME,
  BASED ON WHAT). Silly, community tradition. Port only if it fits
  our tone (the 4-tier rules + "casual-to-MRP" posture in vs-2l2).
  Skip if it feels off-brand.

### Skip
- **media**: static image/file assets for the above cogs. Port
  alongside any cog that needs them.

## Port discipline
- Preserve attribution in the bot's source — a comment block per
  ported feature pointing at the wizard-cogs commit SHA we ported
  from (per our cherry-pick discipline in docs/upstream-sync.md).
- Credit in the bot's README / `/about` slash command.
- License: wizard-cogs is MIT — compatible with our AGPL-3.0 stance
  for the bot code; we can redistribute.

## Acceptance
- [ ] gameserverstatus feature wired as `/status` slash command
- [ ] poweractions features wired as `/restart`, `/stop`, `/update`
      slash commands; admin-gated
- [ ] echo + autoresponder optional per tone decision
- [ ] Attribution + license notice in bot repo

## Dependencies
- Blocks on **vs-2l2** (bot must exist before cogs can be ported)
- Reference source: github.com/space-wizards/wizard-cogs

## Out of scope
- Running RedBot alongside our bot (we pick discord.py for
  consistency; see vs-2l2 scope)
close_reason: Obsolete — scoped a custom Discord bot + wizard-cogs feature port under the assumption vs-2l2 would build its own bot (discord.py). On 2026-04-14 vs-2l2 was updated with a deeper analysis that recommended adopting Red-DiscordBot + wizard-cogs AS-IS, matching the deploy-vanilla-defer-fork pattern used for SS14.Admin, MapServer, cookbook, and RMC14-document-simu (see vs-19h). With no custom bot, there is nothing to port features INTO. File a new fork-wizard-cogs bead only if a real VS14-specific divergence forces it.

title: ops: bootstrap vacation-station-14 website (monorepo at web/)
description:
## Context
VS14 needs a public web presence: landing page explaining the server,
connect instructions, rules, live status, blog/news, credits. Ideally
served from the same host (Caddy) that fronts Grafana and the watchdog,
same TLS cert, same ops pipeline.

Host `vacation.yourdomain.com` (or whatever top-level we pick) as the
player-facing front door. SS14 has no convention-standard server site —
every community runs their own. Examples: deltavstation.com,
wizardsdenaz.io, tg-station-13.org.

## Monorepo placement
```
vacation-station-14/
├── Content.Server/ ...   (existing)
├── web/                  (NEW: this bead)
│   ├── app/              (Next.js 15 app router OR whatever flavor)
│   ├── components/
│   ├── content/          markdown source for rules, about, etc.
│   ├── public/           static assets
│   ├── package.json
│   ├── bun.lock
│   ├── next.config.mjs
│   └── README.md
├── services/ ...
└── ops/ ...
```

`web/` lives alongside the game code. Separate build pipeline (bun / next
build) from the dotnet build. CI adds a web-lint/build job. Deploys to the
same host as the game via systemd + Caddy.

## Pages (minimum viable)

### Public
1. **/** — Landing. Hero: "Vacation Station 14 — hard fork of Delta-V"
   with server status widget (live player count / map / round id pulled
   from `http://51.81.33.136:1212/info` via API route with 15s cache).
   Download launcher button. ss14:// connect button.
2. **/rules** — The rules (rendered from `docs/community/rules.md`, SSOT
   with Discord bot + game MOTD)
3. **/about** — What VS14 is, fork lineage (upstream SS14 → Delta-V → VS14),
   contributors, license (AGPL-3.0 + MIT)
4. **/connect** — Launcher download links, step-by-step first-time-player
   instructions, troubleshooting (auth required, firewall, etc.)
5. **/credits** — Auto-generated from contributors (see vs-39z)
6. **/blog** or **/news** — Tagged markdown posts for announcements,
   patch notes, event recaps. Low-maintenance: write a markdown file,
   push, it ships.

### Player-facing tools (if we fork the ancillary services per vs-19h)
7. **/cookbook** — Crafting recipe browser (if we fork the SS14 cookbook)
8. **/maps** — Map thumbnails + stats (from Content.MapRenderer output)
9. **/docs** — Player-facing docs (if we fork the SS14 docs site into here)

### Admin-facing
10. **/admin** — Auth-gated panel fronted by Wizden OAuth or GitHub. Shows:
    - Live server stats (proxies to internal Grafana)
    - Recent rounds + replays (vs-2l1)
    - Ban list (reads from postgres)
    - Announcement composer (hits watchdog /announce endpoint)

## Tech stack — proposed
- **Next.js 15** (React Server Components + app router) — matches what
  you've already got running (`next-server` seen in `top`). Fastest
  time-to-ship for a SEO-friendly site with live data.
- **bun** as runtime + package manager — matches slack-bot / future
  discord-bot.
- **Tailwind CSS** — no-decision default for rapid theming.
- **shadcn/ui** or similar — component primitives.
- **MDX** for content pages — markdown + React components.
- **No database** on the web side for Phase 1. Reads from: SS14 `/info`
  HTTP, Grafana API (for metrics), existing postgres (read-only for
  admin panel later).

## Integration points
- **Live server status**: API route `/api/server-status` calls
  `http://127.0.0.1:1212/info`, caches 15s, returns JSON. Homepage
  widget consumes it.
- **Bead → blog** auto-post (optional, later): close a bead with a
  `type:announcement` label → post appears under /news.
- **Discord webhook mirror**: new blog post triggers a Discord
  `#announcements` post (bot does the translation).
- **Content sources of truth**: rules.md, motd.md, positioning.md live
  under `docs/community/` in the repo root. Web reads them via FS at
  build time. Discord bot reads them at runtime. Game server reads them
  at restart (via config.toml replacement during deploy).

## Deployment
- systemd unit: `vs14-web.service` — `ExecStart=bun run start` in
  `/home/ubuntu/vacation-station-14/web`
- Port: 3300 (sequential with grafana 3200, staying above the
  3000-collision zone)
- Caddy: `vacation.yourdomain.com` → `127.0.0.1:3300` with automatic HTTPS
- Build step: Content and rebuild on every `git pull` (or CI builds
  ahead of deploy)

## Phased rollout

**Phase 1**: Minimum viable
- Scaffold web/ with Next.js + tailwind
- Home + rules + about + connect + credits pages
- Server-status widget on home
- Caddy routing, systemd unit, deploy script

**Phase 2**: Content pipeline
- MDX blog / news
- Single-source-of-truth integration with Discord bot + game MOTD
  (rules.md / motd.md SSOT)
- Auto-generated credits from git + Patreon (see vs-39z)

**Phase 3**: Integrations
- Embed / link ancillary services (cookbook, maps) per vs-19h outcomes
- Admin panel (gated)

**Phase 4**: Community polish
- SEO metadata + OG tags
- Analytics (self-hosted Plausible or Umami if you care)
- RSS feed for /news

## Dependencies
- **vs-3e3** (content writing) — can ship Phase 1 with placeholder copy
  BUT real launch needs real copy
- **vs-2y8** (Caddy+HTTPS stack active) — web needs Caddy fronting
- **vs-19h** (ancillary services assessment) — determines Phase 3 scope

## Acceptance Criteria (Phase 1)
- [ ] `web/` exists in repo with a Next.js 15 scaffold
- [ ] Home / rules / about / connect / credits pages render locally
- [ ] `/api/server-status` returns live data from SS14 `/info`
- [ ] `vs14-web.service` systemd unit runs via bun
- [ ] Caddyfile block for `vacation.yourdomain.com → :3300` with HTTPS
- [ ] First HTTP 200 served from public domain
- [ ] Lighthouse score reasonable (mobile + desktop ≥80 perf)

## Out of scope for Phase 1
- User accounts / login (Wizden OAuth is Phase 3 admin panel)
- Payments / donations
- In-browser game client (that's SS14's own deal, separate project)
- Realtime presence (needs websocket; later)

## Open questions
- Which domain? You said "yourdomain.com" — pick one before Caddy work.
- Monorepo build tool: pure Next.js or Turborepo/Nx if we go big? Default:
  plain Next.js for Phase 1; adopt Turborepo only if `web/` + `services/discord-bot/`
  start sharing code meaningfully.
- Styling: Tailwind (fast) vs vanilla CSS modules. Default Tailwind.
- Font / brand: needs a design pass. Placeholder: system fonts + a color
  palette chosen quickly.
notes:
## STATE UPDATE — 2026-04-26
Description references "Caddy" + "vacation.yourdomain.com" placeholders. Current reality:

title: ops: community health dashboard (MAU/DAU, retention, game+discord activity)
description:
## Context
Prod observability (vs-2p3) gives us tick rate, player count, memory,
crash rate — operational health. Separate from that, "how healthy is
our community?" is a product question that needs different metrics:
- DAU / MAU trend — retention
- New-player funnel: hub click → connect → first round survived → return next day
- Discord activity — message volume, new member joins, unique posters
- Admin action volume (kicks/bans) as a griefing barometer
- Map / gamemode popularity
- Peak concurrent players (helps decide if we need to scale)

These signals steer decisions: run more events on X map? Tighten auth?
Promote on reddit? Recruit more admins? Open second server?

## Task
1. **Data sources**:
   - Postgres (player accounts, rounds, admin actions) — already have
   - Discord (via discord-bot webhook listener) — need to build
   - Prometheus (Grafana queries) — already have live metrics; add
     retention-shaped derived series
2. **Aggregation**: write rollups into a separate `vacation_station_analytics`
   DB (or a schema) to keep analytics separate from game DB.
   Daily cron aggregates.
3. **Dashboard**: new Grafana dashboard `community-health` imported
   via provisioning (same pattern as vs-13x).
4. **Panels**:
   - DAU / MAU line charts
   - Return-day-N cohorts (bar chart)
   - Discord message volume alongside game activity (correlate spikes)
   - Admin action rate over time
   - Map popularity pie/bar
   - Peak concurrent sessions histogram
5. **Privacy**: aggregate-only data. No individual player tracking
   beyond what's necessary. Document retention policy (see vs-1ux).

## Acceptance
- [ ] Analytics DB / schema created
- [ ] Daily rollup script running via systemd timer
- [ ] Grafana dashboard `community-health` imported + renders
- [ ] Discord message-count collection working
- [ ] Cohort retention chart showing something plausible

## Dependencies
- vs-25k (observability running)
- vs-2l2 (discord-bot Phase 3) for Discord data collection
- vs-1ux (privacy policy) determines what we can / can't aggregate

## Out of scope
- Individual player-tracking dashboards (admin panel via vs-35d can
  show per-player detail for moderation; not duplicated here)
- Churn-prediction ML / fancy models — start with Week-1 numbers

## Notes
- Be boring first: simple SQL rollups + Grafana panels beat elaborate
  analytics platforms. Fancy comes later if/when needed.
- Discord counts are noisy — include bot messages? include #off-topic?
  Document exclusions in the dashboard variable defaults.
notes:
## Closed (2026-04-13)

Scope-as-originally-written was game + Discord activity panels in one dashboard. Game-side landed via child bead vs-2du.1 (12 panels, live at Grafana uid `vs14-community-health`). Discord-side panels are genuinely downstream of vs-2l2 (Discord server + bot) and should be their own bead when Discord data sources exist.

Closing here; file vs-2du-discord or similar when vs-2l2 closes.

title: ops: finish Robust.Cdn integration — CI publish pipeline + cleanup
description:
## Context
vs-3mv (CLOSED 2026-04-13) stood up Robust.Cdn as a docker-compose
service alongside observability at `https://ss14.zig.computer/cdn/`,
added `external/robust-cdn/` submodule + `ops/robust-cdn/` configs, and
switched the watchdog's `UpdateType` from `Local` to `Manifest`
pointing at our CDN's manifest URL.

**What's left is the publishing half:** CI-driven build→publish on
main pushes, plus dead-code cleanup. Leaving these items parked
inside vs-3mv's closed task list was an anti-pattern (closed-bead-
with-undone-work). This bead is the proper follow-up that retires
that gap.

## Current state (verified 2026-04-17)
- ✓ `external/robust-cdn/` submodule present
- ✓ `ops/robust-cdn/` configs (`appsettings.Production.json`)
- ✓ CDN service live: `https://ss14.zig.computer/cdn/fork/vacation-station` → 200
- ✓ Watchdog on `UpdateType: Manifest` pointing at our CDN
- ✗ No CI publishing pipeline writes to our CDN
- ✗ `instances/vacation-station/binaries/` drop-in hack still present (dead code under Manifest mode)
- ✗ `docs/upstream-sync.md` CDN section not updated

## Scope — agent work

### 1. Repoint publish workflows at our CDN
Currently `.github/workflows/publish.yml` + `publish-testing.yml`
default to `wizards.cdn.spacestation14.com` via defaults in
`Tools/publish_multi_request.py`. Repoint:

- **`Tools/publish_multi_request.py`**:
  - `ROBUST_CDN_URL = "https://ss14.zig.computer/cdn/"`
  - `FORK_ID = "vacation-station"` (default; workflow flag still supported)
- **`.github/workflows/publish-testing.yml`**:
  - Uncomment the `schedule: cron` block (my 2026-04-16 `:wrench:`
    commit that disabled it was a stepping stone to this)
  - Update the `--fork-id` default or drop the flag
- **`.github/workflows/publish.yml`**:
  - Decide: do we want this on push to main, or keep it
    workflow_dispatch-only for now? Recommend: push-to-main once
    manual test passes.
- Annotate changed lines with `# VS -` per our upstream-modifications
  convention (so future upstream-sw syncs don't silently clobber).

### 2. Verify CDN publish auth
Check `ops/robust-cdn/appsettings.Production.json` for the auth mechanism
(Robust.Cdn supports bearer tokens via `AuthTokens` or similar). If
a token slot exists but is empty, generate one. If not, add a
section.

### 3. Remove the `binaries/` drop-in hack
`instances/vacation-station/binaries/` becomes dead code the moment
Manifest mode works end-to-end. After step 4 validates, delete the
dir + document the removal.

### 4. Update docs
`docs/upstream-sync.md` — flip the CDN row from "deployed (deferred
integration)" to "fully integrated, CI-driven". Note the VS14
fork-id + manifest URL.

## Scope — human work (mixed bead, clearly called out)

### H1. Generate + register the publish token
- Mint a `PUBLISH_TOKEN` on our CDN instance (configure in
  `ops/robust-cdn/appsettings.Production.json`, restart the service).
- Register it as a **GitHub Actions secret** named `PUBLISH_TOKEN`
  on `azigler/vacation-station-14`.
- Agent cannot do this — needs repo-admin + server-admin access.

### H2. End-to-end test
- After agent lands steps 1–4, manually trigger the publish-testing
  workflow (`gh workflow run publish-testing.yml`).
- Verify: CI runs green → CDN's manifest reports a new version →
  watchdog picks it up on next restart cycle → a fresh launcher
  client downloads from the CDN.
- If anything breaks, loop back to agent for fixes.

### H3. Launch readiness signoff
- Confirm the CDN flow before hub advertisement (vs-17n) — we don't
  want cold inbound launcher traffic with the Local/Manifest
  transition half-wired.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `Tools/publish_multi_request.py` defaults point at our CDN
- [ ] `publish-testing.yml` cron re-enabled, annotated `# VS -`
- [ ] `publish.yml` trigger decided + documented
- [ ] CDN auth configured; `PUBLISH_TOKEN` registered as repo secret (human)
- [ ] End-to-end test passes: CI merge → CDN → watchdog → client (human)
- [ ] `instances/vacation-station/binaries/` removed
- [ ] `docs/upstream-sync.md` CDN row updated

## Dependencies

- Blocks vs-17n (hub advertise) — CDN must be verified before
  cold launcher traffic

## Priority
P2 under vs-2f8 (production ops hardening). Pre-launch priority;
should land before hub advertisement.

title: human: mint PUBLISH_TOKEN + register CDN auth (vs-2f8.1 H1)
description:
## Context
Splits out the H1 human-only task from vs-2f8.1 (closed 2026-04-26).
The agent finished the CI publish wiring; this is the operator action
that activates it. Without this, `gh workflow run publish-testing.yml`
will publish into the void — Robust.Cdn rejects unauthenticated
upload attempts.

## Task
Mint a publish token and wire it into both ends of the pipeline.

### Generate the token
\`\`\`bash
openssl rand -hex 32
\`\`\`

### Server side (Robust.Cdn)
1. Edit `/opt/vacation-station/ops/observability/.env`
2. Add: `CDN_UPDATE_TOKEN=<token>`
3. `cd /opt/vacation-station/ops/observability && sudo docker compose up -d cdn`
4. Verify the env var is loaded:
   \`\`\`bash
   sudo docker compose exec cdn env | grep CDN_UPDATE_TOKEN
   \`\`\`
   The container reads it via `Manifest__Forks__vacation-station__UpdateToken`
   (mapped in `docker-compose.yml`) into the JSON slot the agent added
   in `appsettings.Production.json`.

### GitHub side
1. Open https://github.com/azigler/vacation-station-14/settings/secrets/actions
2. Add a new Actions secret named exactly `PUBLISH_TOKEN` with the
   same value as `CDN_UPDATE_TOKEN`
3. The workflows reference `secrets.PUBLISH_TOKEN`

### Store + audit
- Drop the token into the password manager
- Note the date in the password manager entry; rotate every ~6
  months or after any potential compromise

## Acceptance
- [ ] Token minted (32 hex chars)
- [ ] `CDN_UPDATE_TOKEN` set in `ops/observability/.env`, container
      reloaded, env var visible inside the container
- [ ] `PUBLISH_TOKEN` registered as a GitHub Actions secret on
      `azigler/vacation-station-14`
- [ ] Password-manager entry created
- [ ] Unblocks vs-2f8.11 (end-to-end test)

## Out of scope
- Token rotation runbook (separate bead if/when we ever need it)
- Multi-fork tokens (we only run `vacation-station`)

## Why human-only
Server-admin access to `/opt/`, repo-admin access on GitHub, and a
password-manager entry — agent can't do any of those.

## Source

activates.
