ops: deploy vanilla SS14.Admin with Wizden OAuth + our postgres
description:
## Context
Parent: **vs-19h** (decision matrix + submodule convention).

Deploy space-wizards/SS14.Admin as-is via submodule at
`external/admin/`. VS14-specific config in `ops/admin/`. Stay on
Wizden OAuth per user direction.

## Task
1. Add submodule:
   ```
   git submodule add https://github.com/space-wizards/SS14.Admin external/admin
   git config -f .gitmodules submodule.external/admin.branch master
   git config -f .gitmodules submodule.external/admin.ignore dirty
   ```
2. `ops/admin/`:
   - `docker-compose.yml` — `build: context: ../../external/admin`,
     bind `127.0.0.1:<port>`, EnvironmentFile for secrets.
   - `appsettings.Production.yaml.example` — with:
     ```yaml
     Authentication:
       Oidc:
         Authority: "https://central.spacestation14.io/web/"
         ClientId: "<from Wizden registration>"
         # ClientSecret loaded via env, NOT in file
     ConnectionStrings:
       DefaultConnection: "Host=host.docker.internal;Database=vacation_station;Username=vs14;Password=<env>"
     PathBase: "/admin"
     ```
   - `Caddyfile.block` — `admin.vacation.<domain>` or
     `vacation.<domain>/admin` → `127.0.0.1:<port>` with HTTPS.
3. Register OAuth client with Wizden's identity provider. Store
   ClientId + ClientSecret in `/etc/vacation-station/admin-oauth.env`
   (gitignored). systemd EnvironmentFile loads into the container.
4. Seed initial admin via SQL against `admin` table after first
   migration run (add your Wizden UUID).
5. `docs/OPERATIONS.md` section on admin-panel ops, OAuth client
   rotation, admin-seeding.
6. Update `docs/upstream-sync.md`.

## Acceptance
- [ ] `external/admin/` submodule
- [ ] docker-compose stack boots against live vs14 postgres
- [ ] Wizden OAuth sign-in works
- [ ] ≥1 admin account active
- [ ] Kick / ban / admin-log endpoints functional
- [ ] Caddy-fronted HTTPS
- [ ] OAuth secret in env file, gitignored

## Promotion triggers
- Custom admin panels for VS14-specific features
- UI rebranding beyond config
- Our own identity provider (big, separate)

## Dependencies
- vs-2y8 (Caddy) — admin MUST be HTTPS
- vs-3ty done (postgres)
- OAuth client registered with Wizden

## Security
- Admin panel = high-value target; HTTPS non-optional
- Consider Caddy basic_auth as extra layer on top of OIDC
- Rotate client secret on any suspicion of compromise
- postgres admin user must NOT be superuser; scope grants to what
  SS14.Admin's migrations need
notes:
## Progress 2026-04-13

OAuth registration DONE via Wizden self-service portal (contrary to
earlier assumption that it required manual ask). Creds stashed on
host at ``/etc/vacation-station/admin-oauth.env`` (mode 640,
root:ss14). Do NOT copy these creds into the repo or into systemd
unit text; reference only via EnvironmentFile / docker env_file.

**Rotation-after-deploy**: the secret transited a Claude chat
transcript and should be rotated via the Wizden portal once the
panel is confirmed working. Track as a follow-up.

## First-admin bootstrap (chosen path)

Deploy panel with NO seeded admin. User logs in → OIDC succeeds but
admin-check fails visibly. Operator extracts user's hub UUID from
SS14.Admin logs (``docker compose logs ss14-admin | grep
<username or sub claim>``), seeds via:

    UPDATE admin SET flags = <god-level-mask>
      WHERE user_id = '<uuid>';

Document this in docs/OPERATIONS.md.

## Redirect URI (confirmed)

``https://ss14.zig.computer/admin/signin-oidc`` (per SS14.Admin
README, not the earlier ``/Identity/Account/ExternalLogin`` note).

## DB

Same database as game server: ``vacation_station`` on the host
postgres, owner vs14. SS14.Admin's migrations extend the existing
schema; no separate DB needed.

title: ops: cross-platform nix dev shell (darwin + windows via wsl2)
description:
## Context
The nix flake (`flake.nix`) currently restricts to `x86_64-linux` + `aarch64-linux`. `shell.nix` pulls libdrm/mesa/xorg/gtk3 — all Linux-only — which causes `nix flake check` to fail on darwin. Windows lacks native nix entirely; any nix-based dev path must go through WSL2.

Goal: every platform gets a usable nix-first dev experience, aligned with the first-class nix stance.

## Task

### macOS (darwin): real flake support
1. Split `shell.nix` into platform-aware structure. Options:
   - (a) `shell.nix` takes a `pkgs` arg, branches on `pkgs.stdenv.isDarwin` / `isLinux`, conditionally includes graphics libs.
   - (b) Factor out `shell/common.nix`, `shell/linux.nix`, `shell/darwin.nix`; `shell.nix` selects based on system.
   Prefer (a) — less file sprawl. The branching is `lib.optionals pkgs.stdenv.isDarwin [...] ++ lib.optionals pkgs.stdenv.isLinux [...]`.
2. Darwin-specific deps: `dotnet-sdk_10` still needed. Skip all X11 / mesa / gtk / libdrm / alsa-lib / wayland — they don't exist on darwin. Graphics on mac goes via Apple frameworks, which Robust/RobustToolbox picks up at runtime if it's built to target darwin. Most of those libs may not be needed at all for a SERVER-ONLY darwin dev shell.
3. Decide scope: **server-only** on darwin (no client deps), or attempt client support. Server-only is much simpler and matches the realistic contributor path (client dev on mac needs a proper Mac build of the engine which is a separate problem). Pick server-only and document that mac contributors who need client rendering should use a Linux VM.
4. Re-enable darwin systems in `flake.nix`: `systems = inputs.flake-parts.lib.systems.flakeExposed;` or the explicit list `[ "x86_64-linux" "aarch64-linux" "x86_64-darwin" "aarch64-darwin" ]`.
5. Verify: `nix flake check --no-build --all-systems` passes (evaluates all four systems; darwin devShell pulls fewer deps).

### Windows: WSL2 documentation path
6. No flake changes for Windows — it has no native nix. Windows contributors install WSL2 with Ubuntu, then clone the repo inside WSL and use the standard Linux nix path.
7. Add a "Windows (via WSL2)" subsection to `docs/DEVELOPMENT.md`:
   - Install WSL2: `wsl --install -d Ubuntu-24.04`
   - Inside WSL: install nix (single-user install from https://nixos.org/download), enable flakes, install direnv
   - Clone repo inside WSL filesystem (NOT on Windows drive `/mnt/c/...` — perf disaster)
   - `direnv allow` + standard dev flow
   - Client dev from WSL: GUI apps work via WSLg (Win11+); for audio + OpenGL, this is experimental and may not work reliably. Server-only from WSL is solid.
   - Point macOS contributors who don't want a VM to a similar "server-only nix dev" experience.

### Docs + skill update
8. Update `docs/DEVELOPMENT.md`:
   - Quick Start (Nix) section: mention all three platforms (Linux native, macOS native server-only, Windows via WSL2)
   - Add Windows (via WSL2) subsection
   - Note macOS server-only scope
9. Update `.claude/skills/nix/SKILL.md`:
   - Replace the "Flake is Linux-only" warning with an up-to-date matrix:
     | Platform | Native nix | Client shell | Server shell |
     | Linux    | ✅         | ✅           | ✅           |
     | macOS    | ✅         | ❌ (use VM)  | ✅           |
     | Windows  | ❌ use WSL | ❌           | ✅           |
   - Update the "When to use which path" table accordingly
10. Update `CLAUDE.md` Dev Environment section to remove the Linux-only claim and point at `docs/DEVELOPMENT.md` for platform specifics.

## Out of scope
- Do not attempt to get the full client stack (graphics, audio) working on darwin or WSLg — deep rabbit hole. Document the limitation and move on.
- Do not modify anything outside `shell.nix`, `flake.nix`, docs, and the /nix skill.
- Do not bump `shell.nix` dependency versions beyond what's needed to get darwin to evaluate.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `shell.nix` branches cleanly on `stdenv.isDarwin` / `isLinux`; existing Linux entries unchanged
- [ ] `flake.nix` systems list includes all four (`x86_64-linux`, `aarch64-linux`, `x86_64-darwin`, `aarch64-darwin`)
- [ ] `nix flake check --no-build --all-systems` passes on a Linux host (you may lack a darwin builder — evaluation alone should succeed because flake-parts doesn't require a remote builder for `check`)
- [ ] `docs/DEVELOPMENT.md` has a Windows (WSL2) subsection and updated platform framing
- [ ] `.claude/skills/nix/SKILL.md` has an updated platform support matrix
- [ ] `CLAUDE.md` reflects cross-platform support
- [ ] Single commit, `Bead: vs-35q` trailer, gitmoji `:sparkles:` or `:construction_worker:`

## Notes
- Windows-via-WSL2 is not really "Windows support" — it's "Linux nix running inside a Windows environment." That's fine and honest; just document clearly.
- Darwin users running this on Apple Silicon should get `aarch64-darwin` automatically.
- If `nix flake check` hits a darwin-specific missing dep we can't resolve, it's OK to conditionally exclude darwin from one specific output (e.g. drop `dev-services` on darwin if services-flake has Linux-only assumptions). Document any such exclusions in the matrix.

title: ci: build-docfx.yml fails at engine submodule update
description:
## Context
`.github/workflows/build-docfx.yml` runs on schedule (`0 0 * * 0`, weekly
Sunday midnight). Latest run: **failure at step "Update Engine Submodules"**.
Subsequent steps (dotnet, build, publish docfx) all skipped.

## Probable root cause
The workflow does `git submodule update --init --recursive` then runs
custom engine-update shell. The fork only just got the RobustToolbox
gitlink committed (commit `d80851a3b` during vs-25z). The failure
pre-dates that fix and was running against a repo where the gitlink
didn't exist.

Also: publish step pushes generated docs to GitHub Pages via a PAT
(`secrets.GITHUB_PAT_DOCFX` or similar) — we likely don't have that
secret configured, so even if submodule update succeeded, publish would
fail at the PAT check.

## Investigation needed
1. Confirm whether the next scheduled run (2026-04-19 00:00 UTC)
   succeeds now that the gitlink is committed — if yes, close as fixed.
2. If still failing, inspect the step output — might be one of:
   - Missing engine-update remote / branch
   - Missing GitHub Pages publish secret
   - The workflow hardcodes upstream-specific paths
3. Decide whether we even want auto-published docfx on our fork. We
   don't have a docs site today; this was upstream's pipeline.

## Options
### Option A: disable (like labeler-review)
If we don't serve docfx-generated docs, this is pure upstream noise.
Disable via `gh api .../disable`.

### Option B: fix the secret + submodule path for our fork
Set up GH Pages on `azigler.github.io/vacation-station-14`, create the
PAT, uncomment or add a proper repository guard. Unused today so
mostly busywork.

### Option C: guard with `if: github.repository ==`
Skip on fork, preserve for upstream-sync.

## Recommendation
**A** (disable) for now. If we ever want a docfx site later, we can
revisit — it's a separate decision from "should this workflow run."

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Decision made + recorded
- [ ] If disable: `gh api -X PUT .../disable`, note the workflow id
- [ ] If fix: next scheduled run succeeds, docs live somewhere
- [ ] If guard: fork-case skips cleanly, no failures
notes: Post-Flavor-A: replaced with SS14 upstream's build-docfx.yml. Decision (disable / guard / fix) unchanged — we don't run a docs site. Still needs auditing.

title: ci: update-credits.yml skips on fork by design
description:
## Context
`.github/workflows/update-credits.yml` runs on schedule (weekly Sunday
midnight). Latest run: **skipped**. This is NOT a failure — the workflow
has `if: github.repository == 'DeltaV-Station/Delta-v'`, so every run on
our fork correctly skips the job.

Upstream even left a comment in the file:
```
# Hey there fork dev! If you like to include your own contributors in
# this then you can probably just change this to your own repo
# Do this in dump_github_contributors.ps1 too into your own repo
```

## Options
### Option A: leave it (no action)
Harmless skips every Sunday. Doesn't pollute the failures list. Does
generate a run entry in GitHub Actions history but that's minor.

### Option B: rewrite for VS14 contributors
Flip the guard to our repo, adapt `dump_github_contributors.ps1` to
point at azigler/vacation-station-14. On success, appends new
contributors to our credits/patreons file weekly. Low-value until we
have meaningful contributor traffic.

### Option C: delete
If we're not going to run it, removing reduces workflow file count and
prevents confusion. On upstream-sync, we'd re-delete.

## Recommendation
**A** (leave). Zero cost, zero harm, preserved for future activation.
When we have a few outside contributors and want an auto-updating
credits file, flip to B with a one-line change to the guard + a script
tweak.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Decision recorded
- [ ] If leave: close the bead with "no action, leaving as documented
      skip"
- [ ] If rewrite: guard flipped, ps1 adapted, first run produces a PR
      or commit with current contributors
- [ ] If delete: file removed + added to upstream-sync drop list
notes: Post-Flavor-A: replaced with SS14 upstream's update-credits.yml which guards on 'space-wizards/space-station-14' (not 'DeltaV-Station/Delta-v'). Same 'skips on fork' behavior.

title: human: write rules, MOTD, server positioning, website copy, discord onboarding
description:
## Context
Hub launch, Discord bootstrap, and the website all depend on written
content — the server's identity in words. None of this is code; all of
it is YOUR voice. Can't automate what VS14 stands for.

Currently the committed config.toml.example has placeholder MOTD and no
rules. Discord has no welcome text. Website has no copy. Game MOTD is
blank or upstream default.

Each piece of copy has downstream consumers. Writing in one place and
distributing to all three (game / Discord / website) is the goal (single
source of truth — see vs-2l2 Phase 5 and vs-2dr integrations).

## Deliverables

### 1. Positioning statement (one paragraph)
The 30-second pitch. Goes on:
- Website hero
- Discord `#welcome`
- Hub tags + server description
- `ss14://` server browser blurb

Answer these in order:
- What genre of SS14 server is VS14? (mid-RP? low-RP with ambition?
  PvP-oriented? story-first?)
- What audience? (Veterans burnt out on upstream? Newbies? Delta-V
  refugees?)
- What ONE thing differentiates VS14 from the 50+ other SS14 servers?
- What will you NOT do? (No ERP. No hardcore-RP requirements. Whatever
  the negative-space is.)

Keep under 60 words for the short version; expand to 3 paragraphs for
the about page.

### 2. Server rules (markdown, `docs/community/rules.md`)
Structure (common SS14 pattern, adapt to VS14 voice):
1. **Meta rules** — no ban evasion, no harassment, follow admin
   instructions, how to appeal
2. **Roleplay expectations** — character vs player, IC/OOC separation,
   expected engagement level
3. **Conduct** — no slurs, no bigotry, how to handle conflict
4. **Antag behavior** — acceptable antag play, what crosses the line
5. **Admin escalation** — how to get an admin, what they can do, what
   they won't do
6. **Grief / self-antag** — definitions, consequences
7. **Out-of-server rules** — Discord rules apply equally; community
   extends across both
8. **Metagaming / exploiting** — bugs, client tweaks, third-party tools
9. **Account / verification** — Wizden account expectations

Look at upstream SS14 rules + Delta-V rules + three other good community
servers. Adapt, don't copy. Ban list cites rule numbers, so numbering
matters.

### 3. MOTD (short, `docs/community/motd.md`)
What players see the moment they connect. ~2-4 lines. Usually:
- Server name + fork lineage
- Link to rules
- Link to Discord
- Optional flavor line

Example shape:
```
Welcome to Vacation Station 14 — a hard fork of Delta-V.
Rules: vacation.yourdomain.com/rules | Discord: discord.gg/xxx
Have fun, respect shift structure, break character only in OOC. o7
```

### 4. Website home hero + about page (`web/content/`)
- Hero: 1-sentence pitch + CTA button ("Connect" / "Download launcher")
- About: 3-4 paragraphs — what/who/why, fork lineage, license, how to
  contribute
- Rules page: rendered from `docs/community/rules.md`
- Connect page: launcher download instructions + troubleshooting

### 5. Discord onboarding
- Server description (the short positioning statement)
- `#welcome` pinned message with rules summary + connect instructions
- Rules channel content (rendered from same source as website /rules)
- Role descriptions (what @Admin does, what @Verified is for, etc.)
- Welcome DM to new joiners

### 6. Launch announcement copy
For when you flip the hub advertise switch (vs-17n):
- Tweet / Mastodon / bluesky post
- Discord announcement (both in VS14's own server AND — if you're
  comfortable — in upstream SS14 community spaces)
- Reddit /r/ss14 post (if appropriate)
- Email / DM to Delta-V and other sibling communities for cross-promotion

## Single-source-of-truth layout
```
docs/community/
├── positioning.md          short + long versions
├── rules.md                numbered rules, canonical
├── motd.md                 compressed in-game welcome
├── about.md                 website about-page source
├── launch-announcement.md  copy drafts for launch day
└── discord/
    ├── welcome.md
    ├── roles.md
    └── rules-channel.md    (often the same as rules.md with Discord
                             formatting tweaks)
```

Consumers:
- Game server: deploys `rules.md` + `motd.md` into config.toml cvars
- Discord bot: reads from `docs/community/` at runtime
- Website: imports from `docs/community/` at build time

Edit once, ship three places.

## Writing guidance (not rules — just what tends to work)
- Avoid upstream's passive "X is not allowed"; prefer VS14's voice
  (first-person community voice — "we..." / "here we...")
- Rules should be enforceable; vague rules create drama
- Positioning should close doors ("we are NOT X") as much as open them
- Shorter MOTD is better than longer; players skim
- Humor carefully — what reads as charming to you may read as
  off-putting to a first-timer

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `docs/community/positioning.md` — short + long versions written
- [x] `docs/community/rules.md` — numbered, ≥ 8 sections, enforceable (drafted 2026-05-02)
- [ ] `docs/community/motd.md` — 2-4 lines
- [ ] `docs/community/about.md` — website about page
- [ ] `docs/community/discord/welcome.md` + `roles.md` + `rules-channel.md`
- [ ] `docs/community/launch-announcement.md` — copy for social posts
- [ ] All six consumed by at least one downstream service (once those
      services exist)
- [ ] First proofread pass — fresh eyes read it, flag anything weird

## Out of scope
- Visual brand (logo, color palette, fonts) — separate bead, pairs
  with vs-2dr website Phase 1 styling
- Translated copies (localization) — deferred until we have non-EN
  players asking
- Legal boilerplate (TOS, privacy) — separate bead if we start
  collecting accounts / donations

## Dependencies
None — this is writing. Blocks vs-17n, vs-2l2 Phase 3, vs-2dr Phase 2.

title: epic: VS14 chemistry/medical/cryo companion app (first-party tool)
description:
## Context

VS14's first original player-facing tool: a chemistry + medical + cryo
companion web app designed for rapid in-game use by chemists and medics.
Inspired by [bugmedical](https://hoshizora-sayo.github.io/bugmedical/)
(reference-only; we won't reuse its source due to no-license-declared
ambiguity) + structurally mirrored to the cookbook (`external/cookbook/`,
vs-1vy) so "understand one, understand the other."

**Positioning:** our first foray into building branded VS14 tooling for
the SS14 community. Designed so other servers could adopt it too.

## Architecture

### Repo layout (mirror cookbook exactly)
1. **New GitHub repo** (author: VS14) — needs to be created as part of
   this work. Suggested slug: `azigler/<name>` (final name TBD — see
   Open Questions).
2. **Submodule into `external/<name>/`** — same slot as `external/cookbook/`.
3. **`ops/<name>/`** holds our deploy config (`build.sh`, `install.sh`,
   nginx block, systemd oneshot+timer mirroring `vs14-cookbook-build.service`).
4. **Public URL**: `https://ss14.zig.computer/<name>/` (nginx path-based
   routing, same pattern as `cookbook/` and `guidebook/`).

### Tech stack (match cookbook)
- TypeScript + Rollup, JSX (no React dep) — preserves the
  "understand one, understand the other" principle.
- Fluent for any future i18n slots.
- Pure static output — no backend. `public/` dir is what nginx serves.
- Node 20+ / npm for build.
- License: **AGPLv3** (matches our other first-party code; matches cookbook).

### Data pipeline (mirror cookbook's `gen/`)
Parse SS14 YAML at build time, emit static JSON the frontend loads:
- **Reagent prototypes** — `Resources/Prototypes/Reagents/**/*.yml`
  → chem name, ID, color, metabolism rate, effects (reactive groups),
  OD threshold, heat capacity.
- **Reaction prototypes** — `Resources/Prototypes/Recipes/Reactions/**/*.yml`
  → ingredients, products, catalysts, temperature requirements, mix order.
- **Damage types** — which reagent heals which damage type + rate.
- **Hazard metadata** — razorium-style combinations (auto-surfaced from
  reaction data where possible; manually curated for the rest).
- **Container specs** — jug/bottle/beaker prototypes: capacity, max
  reagents, labelable.
- **Sprites** — reagent/container icons from SS14 RSI, same spritesheet
  approach cookbook uses.

Uses VS14's own game-data clone as source (same `sources.yml` pattern as
cookbook). Keeps us authoritative against our actual gameplay.

## User-facing scope

### Tier 1 — reference (bugmedical-plus)
Three top-level sections mirroring bugmedical's structure:

1. **Medical** — Brute / Toxin / Burn / Airloss / Genetic damage.
   Per-damage-type: list of healing reagents with dosage, healing
   amount/rate, OD threshold, warnings (razorium-type interactions),
   icon.
2. **Chemistry** — full recipe cards (like cookbook): inputs,
   temperature, catalysts, outputs. Searchable + filterable.
3. **Cryo** — cryo-specific procedures: cryoxadone stack, beaker setup,
   freezer temperature targets, emergency stabilization flows.

All three pages cross-link the same underlying data — a reagent page
shows both its healing uses + its recipe.

Plus "Pro Tips" — carry forward the bugmedical pro-tips idea as a
callouts layer (admin-editable curation file checked into the repo).

### Tier 2 — in-game ergonomics

- **Search bar** — reagent-name autocomplete, fuzzy matching.
- **Copy-label** — per reagent: copy a pre-formatted label string
  (`"Tricordrazine / 30u / 2026-04-18 / made by ..."`) to clipboard.
  Per mix-group: copy a multi-line label batch. Settings: operator
  fills their in-game name once, it auto-populates labels.
- **Keyboard-first UX** — `/` to search, arrow keys to navigate,
  `c` to copy, `esc` to close. Chemists in-game are often typing
  fast with the game window active.

### Tier 3 — mix-group planner (localStorage)

- Chemists often prep batches: "I need X amount of Tricord, Y amount of
  Dylovene, Z amount of Bicaridine."
- Planner lets you queue multiple reagents, specify desired final volume
  per batch, and outputs:
  - **Total ingredients** summed across the group (list of raw chems +
    units).
  - **Optimal order** (temperature-sensitive reactions first, etc.).
  - **Container plan** — settings for jugs/beakers/droppers, auto-tiled
    to fit the chosen container count + capacity.
  - **Label export** — batch-copy all labels at once.
- Groups persist in **localStorage** (no backend, no auth).
- Share-URL option: mix-group encoded in URL fragment so a chemist can
  DM a teammate a prepared batch link.

## Dependencies

- vs-1vy (cookbook) — live reference, same YAML parsing lib stack
- vs-2y8 (nginx+TLS) — ✓ DONE, nginx is up
- SS14 game data — available locally via our main repo clone

## Acceptance criteria

### Repo + ops
- [ ] New GitHub repo created under azigler/ (or chosen org)
- [ ] Repo submoduled at `external/<name>/` with `ignore = dirty`
- [ ] `ops/<name>/` contains build script + install script + nginx block
- [ ] `vs14-<name>-build.service` + `.timer` mirror cookbook's pattern
- [ ] `docs/upstream-sync.md` row added

### Data
- [ ] `gen/` pipeline parses reagents, reactions, damage types from SS14 YAML
- [ ] Container/jug data extracted
- [ ] Razorium-style hazard data modeled (auto + manual)
- [ ] Spritesheet generated for reagent + container icons
- [ ] Output `public/data/*.json` + sprites ready to ship

### Frontend
- [ ] Three section pages: Medical, Chemistry, Cryo
- [ ] Reagent detail view (healing uses + recipe + hazards + icon)
- [ ] Search + filter across all reagents
- [ ] Copy-label (per reagent + per mix group) with operator-name pref
- [ ] Keyboard shortcuts: `/`, arrows, `c`, `esc`
- [ ] Mix-group planner with localStorage persistence
- [ ] Shareable URL-fragment mix-groups
- [ ] Pro Tips layer (curated callouts)
- [ ] Responsive (works on narrow windows alongside in-game client)

### Deploy
- [ ] Live at `https://ss14.zig.computer/<name>/` returning 200
- [ ] systemd timer rebuilds on a daily schedule (picks up game-data updates)
- [ ] nginx location block loaded + tested

### Docs
- [ ] Repo README (usage, build, contributing)
- [ ] Privacy policy template (cookbook has `privacy.example.html` — mirror)
- [ ] Attribution for SS14 sprites + upstream inspiration (bugmedical credit)

## Open Questions (for /review)

### OQ-1: Name
Three candidates; user picks one in /review:
- **Dispensary** — direct, parallel to "Cookbook"
- **Bedside** — medical companion feel
- **Nurseshark** — most on-brand with Vacation Station's tropical vibe

My bias: Nurseshark — distinctive, brand-true, memorable.

### OQ-2: GitHub org
- **`azigler/<name>`** — matches existing VS14 repo ownership
- **Dedicated org** (`vs14-dev/`, `vacation-station/`) — future-proofs
  for multi-maintainer
- My bias: stay with `azigler/<name>` until multi-maintainer need appears.

### OQ-3: Mix-group planner — in MVP or Phase 2?
Tier 3 is real engineering (maybe 20-30% of total work). Options:
- **Ship Tier 1+2 as v0.1**, file Tier 3 as a follow-up bead
- **Ship full Tier 1+2+3 as v1.0** — longer runway to first demo
- My bias: Tier 1+2 first (reference + copy-label + search), then
  Tier 3 in a follow-up — user-visible value lands sooner.

### OQ-4: Attribution to bugmedical
We're not forking their code, but their reference guide was the catalyst
for this tool. Options:
- **Silent** — no mention
- **Credit in /about or README** — "Inspired by hoshizora-sayo/bugmedical"
- My bias: explicit credit. Good internet citizenship costs us nothing.

### OQ-5: Homepage integration
vs-2dr (website) is still OPEN. Options:
- **Ship this tool now at `ss14.zig.computer/<name>/`**, vs-2dr links to it
  when the homepage exists
- **Wait for vs-2dr to land first** so the tool ships alongside a homepage
- My bias: ship now. Tool has standalone value; doesn't need the homepage.

### OQ-6: Pro Tips curation
Where does the Pro Tips content come from?
- **Auto-extract** from game data where possible (e.g. common-mistake flags
  in reagent metadata)
- **Hand-curated** in a markdown file checked into the tool repo
- **Hybrid** — auto where possible, manual override
- My bias: hybrid, starting mostly manual with hooks for auto-extraction.

## Out of scope

- Cryo equation solver (temperature simulation) — maybe Phase 3
- Food/drink recipes — that's cookbook's domain; we cross-link
- Surgery guides — different axis, separate tool if ever built
- Admin tooling (spawning, banning) — SS14.Admin covers that
- Multi-language / i18n content translation — i18n scaffolding present
  (Fluent) but only English ships v1
- Mobile app — web-first, PWA-ready is enough
close_reason: Epic complete. Nurseshark — VS14's first original player-facing tool — is LIVE at https://ss14.zig.computer/nurseshark/. All 11 children closed across data pipeline, frontend, Rx solver (damage-to-mix + revival flow), species sprites, physical-items YAML, blacklist, arachnid copper overlay, side-effect warnings, wiki-canonical pro-tips, and vitest cleanup. Tech stack: Vite + React + TypeScript, AGPLv3, static deploy via systemd + nginx with path-based routing. Nightly rebuild timer fires 05:30 UTC. 89 vitest tests pass. Inspirations: SS14 Cookbook (structure), bugmedical (content organization), SS14 wiki (canonical voice). No public announcement per user direction. Two P3 follow-ups filed for monitoring + rsync backup.

title: feat: nurseshark physical-items — verify/extract healing amounts from VS14 YAML
description:
## Context
vs-2wj's solver shipped with hand-modeled physical-item heal amounts (Bandage 10 Bloodloss + 5 Blunt, Gauze 15 Bloodloss, Ointment 10 Heat, Regenerative Mesh 15 Heat + 10 Shock, Medicated Suture 10 Blunt + 10 Piercing + 10 Slash, Blood Pack 50 Bloodloss with ironMetabolism flag).

These are reasonable defaults — subagent explicitly flagged they aren't verified against VS14 YAML. The solver's physical-composition accuracy depends on real numbers.

## Scope
1. Grep Resources/Prototypes/Entities/Objects/Specific/Medical/ in VS14 for the medical items.
2. Each should have a HealingComponent (or equivalent) with damage types, amounts, stack counts.
3. Either:
   a) Extract at build-time via src/gen/resolve-physical-items.ts emitting public/data/physical-items.json, refactor src/data/physical-items.ts to load from it.
   b) Hand-update PHYSICAL_ITEMS with verified numbers, document the source YAML path in comments.
4. Add test fixtures covering the verified values.

Approach (a) is cleaner (data pipeline stays source of truth); (b) is faster. Recommend (a).

## Acceptance
- [ ] Physical items data sourced from VS14 YAML or manually verified
- [ ] Solver produces accurate physical-item counts for worked examples
- [ ] Tests reflect verified numbers

## Priority
P3 — cosmetic accuracy. Solver composition logic is correct; per-item heal amounts may be off by a few units.

title: feat: nurseshark reagent blacklist — hide uncraftable/admin-only reagents (Rororium first)
description:
## Context
Solver's v1.0 shipped (vs-2wj). For 45 Blunt / Human input, it picked **Rororium** as the healing reagent — a real reagent in `Resources/Prototypes/Reagents/chemicals.yml`, group `Biological`, that heals 4 Brute/tick AND grants 120s adrenaline. Characteristics:
- **No reactions produce it** (uncraftable via Chemistry dept)
- Group is `Biological`, not `Medicine`
- Effectively admin-spawn or special-encounter content, not something a player chemist can synthesize

Surfacing rare/unsynthable reagents in the solver output misleads medics into thinking they should be making it. Need a curated exclusion list.

Also applies to the reagent reference browser: a "normal play" view should hide these, while an "include admin/rare" toggle shows everything.

## Scope

### 1. Build the blacklist data
Create `src/data/reagent-blacklist.ts` (or emit from the data pipeline as `public/data/reagent-blacklist.json` if preferred — pipeline-backed is more future-proof):

```typescript
interface BlacklistEntry {
  id: string;
  reason: "uncraftable" | "admin-only" | "syndicate-only" | "botany-only" | "special-event" | "other";
  notes: string;  // "no reactions produce it"
}
```

Seed with `Rororium` (uncraftable, pure-play not available). Then **sweep the data** to find siblings:
- Reagents in `Resources/Prototypes/Reagents/*.yml` with **no reactions producing them** AND not in the roundstart chem dispenser base element list.
- Reagents in groups like `Narcotic`, `Syndicate`, `Admin`, or the handful in `fun.yml` (Razorium is already a warning; others may need similar flagging).
- Reagents referenced in `Resources/Prototypes/Objects/Specific/SyndicateSynthesis/` or admin/ghost-role chemistry kits.

Write a one-off `npm run sweep:unreachable-reagents` script (or a `scripts/` helper) that lists every reagent not producible by any reaction in the non-admin reaction dataset. Prune by hand + annotate reasons.

### 2. Solver integration
In `src/data/solver.ts`, filter candidate reagents through the blacklist before the ranking step:
- By default, blacklisted reagents are never picked.
- Add an `includeRestricted: boolean` field to `SolverInput` (default `false`).
- Warning if solver would have picked a blacklisted reagent but couldn't due to the filter: "Best match (Rororium) is uncraftable — falling back to [Bicaridine]."

### 3. Reagent browser integration  
On `/reagents` grid:
- Default view hides blacklisted.
- Add a toggle "Show admin / rare reagents" at the top of the list.
- Per-reagent card: badge with the restriction reason if shown.

### 4. Documentation
`nurseshark/CLAUDE.md` gets a short section on the blacklist + how to add entries.

## Acceptance
- [ ] `src/data/reagent-blacklist.ts` (or pipeline JSON) lists Rororium + every other reagent not reachable via reactions in the non-admin dataset
- [ ] Sweep script documented + reproducible
- [ ] Each entry has a reason + notes
- [ ] Solver skips blacklisted candidates by default
- [ ] Solver surfaces the "best match was restricted, used X instead" warning when relevant
- [ ] Reagent browser has the include-restricted toggle

title: feat: nurseshark arachnid copper overlay — fix species-specific Bloodloss handling (wiki correctness)
description:

title: feat: nurseshark side-effect warnings — surface Ultravasculine brute, Arithrazine brute, Tricord <50, Epi critical-only

title: feat: nurseshark revival flow — dead-patient solver mode (topicals → defib → post-revival chems)
description:
## Context
Wiki (Medical): "you will first need to ensure that their Total Damage is below 200 points by using Topical Treatments (see table below). Then, grab a Defibrillator, turn it on (press z), then use it on the patient to shock them back to life. This will bring them back to critical condition, allowing chemicals to be used to heal the remainder of their damage."

The current solver is patient-alive-only — it optimizes for ongoing treatment with chemicals. Dead patients need a DIFFERENT flow:
1. **Drop total damage below 200** using topicals (chemicals don't metabolize in dead patients)
2. **Defibrillate** (the defib itself heals up to 40 asphyxiation, inflicts 5 shock)
3. **Post-revival**: patient is in critical condition; now normal chemical treatment applies

This is a distinct solver mode. Topicals are the only tool; chemicals don't work on corpses.

## Scope

### 1. New input: patient state
Add to `SolverInput`:
- `patientState: "alive" | "critical" | "dead"` — default "alive"
- When `"dead"`, the solver switches to revival mode:
  - Only considers physical items (topicals)
  - Target: reduce total damage to <200
  - Output includes a **"defibrillate now"** step once target is reached
  - Post-revival: emits a follow-up mix targeting any remaining damage (this is the chemical portion, just labeled "post-revival chems")

### 2. Topical-only composition
Reuse the physical-items data. For each damage type, pick topicals greedily until either:
- Total remaining damage < 200 → emit "defibrillate now" step
- No more topicals can help (e.g. Holy damage on a corpse — can't revive with current tooling → warning "Patient cannot be revived via available topicals; consult CMO")

### 3. Defib step representation
New output field: `revivalStep: { tool: "defibrillator"; heals: { Asphyxiation: 40 }; inflicts: { Shock: 5 }; note: "Press Z to activate, then use on patient." }` — shown as a distinct third panel, not an ingredient.

### 4. Post-revival chems
After the revival step, if the patient's (projected) post-revival state has damage, emit a normal solver output for that state — labeled "Follow-up chemicals (post-revival)".

### 5. UI reshaping
- Add a "patient state" dropdown to the solver form: Alive / Critical / Dead. Default Alive.
- When Dead: form UI shifts — physical/cryo toggles stay, chems toggle becomes "post-revival chems" toggle.
- Output renders three panels: Topicals → Defib → Post-revival chems.

### 6. Tests
- Dead patient with 180 total damage → defib immediately, post-revival chems panel
- Dead patient with 250 total damage → topicals list to reduce to <200, then defib, then post-revival chems
- Dead patient with 400 total damage that can't be reduced below 200 with available topicals → "cannot revive" warning
- Alive/Critical patient unchanged (regression coverage)

## Acceptance
- [ ] `SolverInput.patientState` added + wired
- [ ] Dead-patient mode produces topicals → defib → follow-up chems
- [ ] Defib step distinct from ingredients panel
- [ ] UI dropdown for patient state
- [ ] Warning when revival impossible
- [ ] 4+ new test scenarios pass

## Priority
P2 — meaningful feature parity with in-game medic workflow.

## Dispatch
Medium scope; ~3-4 hours. Shares solver.ts with other in-flight nurseshark beads, so dispatch after they land to avoid merge conflicts.
close_reason: Verified closed — work landed at nurseshark 3f88c1b (merged main). Revival flow: topicals → damage<200 → defib → recursive post-revival chem solve. 89/89 tests pass. Reopened by subagent state-touch after prior close; re-closed in orient.

title: content: nurseshark pro-tips expansion — fold in wiki-canonical content with [verified-wiki] tag
description:
## Context

- [verified-wiki] Three actions for bleeding: (1) stop bleeding [gauze / tranexamic acid], (2) restore blood level [Iron or Saline; Copper for Arachnids], (3) cure bloodloss damage [Dexalin Plus].
- [verified-wiki] Tranexamic Acid: 3× stronger than Pulped Banana Peel, 6× stronger than Inaprovaline for bleed reduction.

**Defibrillator**:
- [verified-wiki] Heals up to 40 asphyxiation; inflicts 5 shock. Requires patient total damage <200. Press Z to activate.

**Tricordrazine**:
- [verified-wiki] "Only works below 50 total damage." Heals 1 brute + 0.5 poison + 1 burn per unit. Fallback when better meds unavailable.

**Epinephrine quirk**:

**Dermaline OD top-up trick**:

**Species-specific** (the wiki calls these out clearly):

- [verified-wiki] Medibots: default inject Tricordrazine (minor) or Inaprovaline (critical). Wrench-anchor near medical beds for autonomous triage.

**Zombie cure**:
- [verified-wiki] Ambuzol (dylovene + ammonia + zombie blood) cures zombie infection. Ambuzol+ (ambuzol + omnizine) grants permanent immunity. Bite while in critical state = instant zombification.

**Chemical delivery methods**:
- [verified-wiki] Pills up to 20u, slower onset (digestion). Syringes up to 15u, near-instant. CMO hypospray: 30u capacity, 5u doses, instant.

### 3. Source attribution footer

### 4. UI updates

### 5. Tests

- Callout renders correct color
- Filter chip works

## Acceptance

P3 — content enrichment. Not blocking public launch but significantly improves utility.

Sources footer with 4 wiki URLs. Parser + callout + chip extended for new tag (violet). 14/14 tests pass. Wiki-faithful voice preserved: near-direct quotes for core claims (damage <200 for revival, 300u baseline blood, 10× stasis metabolism), paraphrased-yet-faithful for rest. title: fix: nurseshark vitest exclude worktree paths (phantom test-suite failures)
description:
## Context
Multiple nurseshark subagents (vs-3il.4, vs-3il.7) have reported that vitest's default test discovery picks up test files from sibling worktree clones at `/home/ubuntu/nurseshark/.claude/worktrees/agent-*/src/**/__tests__/*.test.ts`. These show up as "phantom" failed suites in `npm run test` output, confusing the real test signal.

Fix is trivial: add an `exclude` pattern to `vite.config.ts`'s test config.

## Scope
`/home/ubuntu/nurseshark/vite.config.ts` — extend the `test:` block:
```ts
test: {
  environment: 'jsdom',
  globals: true,
  setupFiles: ['./src/test/setup.ts'],
  exclude: [
    '**/node_modules/**',
    '**/dist/**',
    '**/.{idea,git,cache,output,temp}/**',
    '**/worktrees/**',  // NEW: ignore symlinked-in worktree test files
  ],
},
```

## Acceptance
- [ ] `npm run test` runs clean (no phantom failed suites from worktrees)
- [ ] Tests in `/src/` still all discovered + run

## Priority
P3 — quality-of-life for running tests. No user impact.

## Dispatch
~5 minute edit. Can ship as a quick subagent or inline.
close_reason: Vitest exclude shipped at nurseshark 9c2f6ff. 9 phantom failed suites → 0. Still 89/89 real tests pass. exclude pattern covers node_modules, dist, git/cache/output/temp, AND **/worktrees/**. Curious surprise: vite was resolving the worktree paths against vacation-station-14's filesystem root instead of nurseshark's — explaining why they were phantom (unresolvable). Pattern sidesteps the whole mess regardless.

title: ops: stand up Robust.Cdn + switch watchdog UpdateType to Manifest (deferred)
description:
## Context
Parent: **vs-19h** (decision matrix + submodule convention) — DEFERRED.

When triggered, deploy space-wizards/Robust.Cdn via submodule at
`external/cdn/`. VS14-specific config in `ops/cdn/`. Pairs with
watchdog's Manifest update provider (we currently use Local).

## Why deferred
Local update provider works fine for single-server. Manifest requires
Robust.Cdn + CI + TLS + watchdog reconfiguration — real work but not
blocking day-one.

## Triggers to unpark
- Multiple VS14 servers (staging + prod, or cross-region)
- Frequent content updates making zip-drops painful
- Player bandwidth / latency complaints downloading client
- "Join via launcher without operator intervention" workflow

## Task (when triggered)
1. Submodule:
   ```
   git submodule add https://github.com/space-wizards/Robust.Cdn external/cdn
   ```
2. `ops/cdn/`:
   - `docker-compose.yml`
   - `appsettings.yaml` — content publish path, signing keys
     (env-loaded), manifest path
   - `Caddyfile.block` — `cdn.vacation.<domain>` with HTTPS
3. CI pipeline: on main push, package + upload to CDN's publish
   endpoint, bump manifest version
4. Watchdog config update:
   ```yaml
   UpdateType: Manifest
   Updates:
     ManifestUrl: https://cdn.vacation.<domain>/manifest.json
   ```
5. Remove the `binaries/` drop-in hack
6. `docs/upstream-sync.md` updated

## Acceptance (when triggered)
- [ ] `external/cdn/` submodule
- [ ] CDN running, Caddy-fronted, TLS
- [ ] CI publishes client on main push
- [ ] Watchdog on Manifest provider
- [ ] Clients download from CDN on connect

## Dependencies
- vs-2y8 (Caddy)
- CI that actually builds the client on push
notes:
## Service live (2026-04-13)

CDN deployed as a docker-compose service alongside observability.
Reachable at https://ss14.zig.computer/cdn/fork/vacation-station.
No builds uploaded yet; manifest endpoint returns 404 until the
first publish.

### Remaining work (to fully flip production to Manifest mode)

2. **Flip watchdog UpdateType: Local → Manifest**

3. **Restart watchdog; smoke-test launcher**

### Automation — next publish

Add a post-build hook to Content.Packaging: after it produces

title: ops: guidebook — render reagent/microwave/tech/lawset embeds as tables (not pills)
description:
## Context vs-1e5 shipped the guidebook; vs-mlg added entity sprite rendering. What's left: pages like Chemicals, FoodRecipes, PizzaRecipes, etc. still show empty pills for group embeds. The in-game renderer expands these to tables (reagent list, recipe list, tech tree, lawset text). Web-side just has `Name`. Audit of embed tags in ``Resources/ServerInfo/Guidebook/**/*.xml`` (still falling back to pills post-vs-mlg): | Tag | Count | Source prototype | |-------------------------------|-------|-----------------------------------------------------------| | ``GuideReagentEmbed`` | 42 | ``type: reagent`` in Resources/Prototypes/Reagents/ | | ``GuideReagentGroupEmbed`` | 22 | reagents grouped by their ``group:`` field | | ``GuideMicrowaveGroupEmbed`` | 30 | ``type: microwaveMealRecipe`` grouped by ``group:`` field | | ``GuideTechDisciplineEmbed`` | 4 | ``type: technology`` + ``type: techDiscipline`` | | ``GuideLawsetListEmbed`` | 1 | ``type: siliconLawset`` | ## Task Extend `ops/guidebook/render.py` to expand each of these embeds into a table (or similar structured layout) instead of a pill. Match the information density of the in-game version — we don't need pixel-perfect styling, but we do need the data. ### Per-tag design sketches - **GuideReagentEmbed**: single row — sprite (if any), name, description, metabolism / color / physicalDesc summary if they're short. - **GuideReagentGroupEmbed**: table of all reagents whose ``group:`` matches. Columns: icon, name, short description. Filter by the ``Group="..."`` attribute. - **GuideMicrowaveGroupEmbed**: table of all microwave recipes matching ``group:``. Columns: result entity (with sprite via vs-mlg resolver), inputs (list of reagent + solid counts), time. - **GuideTechDisciplineEmbed**: list of technologies in that discipline. Nested or flat is fine. Show name + cost + tier. - **GuideLawsetListEmbed**: show the lawset's name + the ordered list of law strings. ### Implementation notes - Reuse the existing entity-prototype scan from vs-mlg; just add reagent / recipe / technology scans alongside it. Single-pass YAML walk. - Reagent sprites come from the ``iconPath`` / ``metamorphicSprite`` fields, or fall back to the entity this reagent is stored in. Don't over-engineer — "sprite if easy, skip otherwise" is fine for v1. - Locale: reagent + recipe names live in ``Resources/Locale/en-US/**/*.ftl`` keyed by ``reagent-name-`` and similar. Resolve through the same FTL loader already used for guidebook entry titles. - Keep degraded rendering: if a group is empty (no reagents match), fall back to the pill so we don't silently ship empty tables. - CSS: add simple ``table.embed-table { ... }`` rules. Match the dark aesthetic already in style.css. ## Acceptance - [ ] Visit ``/guidebook/Chemicals.html`` — each ``

`` section (Elements, Medicine, Narcotics, …) is followed by a table of reagents with at least name + description - [ ] Visit ``/guidebook/PizzaRecipes.html`` (and other recipe pages) — recipes shown as a table with result sprite + inputs - [ ] Visit ``/guidebook/Technologies.html`` — 4 discipline sections each show a list of their technologies - [ ] ``GuideLawsetListEmbed`` on the one page that uses it renders the law text - [ ] Build time stays under 2 minutes - [ ] shellcheck + ruff clean - [ ] Fallback pill still works for unresolvable embeds ## Out of scope (file follow-ups if needed) - Full reagent-reaction chemistry graphs (the in-game version shows reaction formulas — defer unless trivial) - Gas embeds (``GuideGasEmbed`` — none used currently) - Multi-layer reagent sprite compositing ## Parent vs-z7v (community launch readiness)

title: fix: grafana postgres datasource type mismatch across prod + dev
description:
## Context
vs-2p3 + vs-13x shipped conflicting datasource types for Postgres in Grafana:

- `ops/observability/docker-compose.yml:107` env `GF_INSTALL_PLUGINS: grafana-postgresql-datasource` — installs the plugin
- `ops/observability/grafana/provisioning/datasources/datasources.yml:29` — provisions datasource with `type: postgres` (built-in)
- `ops/observability/grafana/dashboards/game-servers.json:41` (and panels in perf-metrics.json) — references `"type": "grafana-postgresql-datasource"` (plugin)

When Grafana provisions a datasource with `type: postgres` but a panel asks for `type: grafana-postgresql-datasource`, the panel fails to locate a matching datasource. In the dev services-flake stack the plugin isn't installed at all — no fallback there either.

This will silently break the Connections panel on Game Servers and any postgres-querying panel on Perf Metrics when the operator runs vs-205 verification.

## Task
Pick ONE datasource type and make all three surfaces agree. Recommend `grafana-postgresql-datasource` (the plugin) for parity with upstream SS14 dashboards — postgres-as-plugin offers query builder + TimescaleDB hooks the built-in lacks, and upstream dashboards were authored against it.

### Changes required

1. **`ops/observability/grafana/provisioning/datasources/datasources.yml`**: change Postgres block `type: postgres` → `type: grafana-postgresql-datasource`. Verify the rest of the block (jsonData, secureJsonData) is still compatible with the plugin schema (it should be — the plugin is a drop-in successor).

2. **`ops/observability/docker-compose.yml`**: confirm `GF_INSTALL_PLUGINS: grafana-postgresql-datasource` is correctly spelled and the plugin installs on grafana 11.3.0 startup. If the plugin requires a specific minimum grafana version, document it. No code change needed unless the image pin is too old.

3. **Dashboards** (`game-servers.json`, `perf-metrics.json`): already reference `grafana-postgresql-datasource` — no change needed. Do grep-verify that NO panel still references `type: postgres` by mistake; if any do, fix.

4. **Dev services-flake stack** (`flake.nix` `perSystem.process-compose."dev-services".services.grafana.graf1`): the plugin isn't in nixpkgs `grafanaPlugins`. Two options:
   - **(a) Install at runtime**: add `GF_INSTALL_PLUGINS=grafana-postgresql-datasource` as an env var / arg to the dev grafana so it fetches the plugin from grafana.com on first start. Services-flake grafana module may expose this via `services.grafana.graf1.settings.plugin_install` or `extraEnv`/`env`. Check the module.
   - **(b) Omit postgres in dev**: drop the Postgres datasource from the dev flake entirely and have contributors use Prometheus + Loki only in dev. Dashboards' postgres panels would show "no datasource" in dev but that's acceptable if documented.

   Prefer **(a)** if the services-flake grafana module supports runtime plugin install; otherwise fall back to **(b)** and document clearly in `docs/DEVELOPMENT.md` Dev Services Stack section.

5. **Cross-ref comment sync**: `ops/observability/grafana/provisioning/datasources/datasources.yml` and the dev flake's inlined grafana datasources should each carry a comment pointing at the other as the "also update me" sibling — reduces drift risk (finding #2 from vs-1bb).

### Validation
- `docker compose -f ops/observability/docker-compose.yml config` parses
- `python -c "import yaml; yaml.safe_load(open('ops/observability/grafana/provisioning/datasources/datasources.yml'))"` parses
- Each dashboard JSON still parses
- If option (a) chosen: `nix flake check --no-build --all-systems` passes
- Grep the repo for any remaining `type: postgres` references that should have been updated (and any `grafana-postgresql-datasource` that shouldn't have been touched — the dashboards are correct as-is)

### Commit
One commit, gitmoji `:bug:`, trailer `Bead: vs-3oe`.

## Out of scope
- Do not change image pins unless strictly required by plugin compatibility
- Do not rewrite the dashboard JSONs structurally (they're canonical as vs-13x landed them)
- Do not migrate off `grafana-postgresql-datasource` to another postgres backend

## References
- Plugin page: https://grafana.com/grafana/plugins/grafana-postgresql-datasource/
- services-flake grafana module: https://community.flake.parts/services-flake/services/grafana

title: legal: license audit for all bundled / deployed services + LEGAL.md update
description:
## Context
We're about to deploy / bundle code from multiple upstream repositories
alongside our own fork. Each has its own license, and our obligations
differ per service (AGPL = network-service copyleft; MIT = attribution
only). Need a careful audit before public launch, not after.

**Additional context from user direction**: mirror HardLight's
README-level transparency and attribution pattern
(https://github.com/HardLightSector/HardLight/blob/master/README.md).
They do this extremely well; we should copy the pattern beat-for-beat.

## HardLight's transparency pattern — our target

### Pattern 1: Commit-hash license boundaries
HardLight documents in their README:

> "Content contributed to this repository after commit
> 2fca06eaba205ae6fe3aceb8ae2a0594f0effee0 is licensed under the GNU
> Affero General Public License version 3.0"
>
> "Content contributed to this repository before commit
> 2fca06eaba205ae6fe3aceb8ae2a0594f0effee0 is licensed under the MIT
> license"

Clean, unambiguous, machine-traceable. Anyone wanting to know what
license applies to a given file or line can run `git log --follow
<path>` and compare commit SHAs against the boundary.

### Pattern 2: Per-upstream attribution table
HardLight's README has a table with columns:
- **Subdirectory** (e.g., `_NF`, `_DV`, `_Corvax`, `_EE`)
- **Fork Name** (Frontier Station, Delta-V, Corvax, Einstein Engines)
- **Fork Repository** (URL)
- **License** (AGPL 3.0, MIT, etc.)

One row per upstream we pull from, in one place readers can scan.

### Pattern 3: Modification markers
HardLight says:
> "When we pull content from other forks, we organize their content to
> repo-specific subfolders to better track attribution and limit merge
> conflicts."
>
> "These modifications are denoted by comments around the modified
> lines."

Which maps to: `_NF/` etc. for self-contained code; inline `// NF`
comments for upstream-file modifications. Same convention we already
use for `_VS` / `_DV` — extend to every upstream we adopt.

## Task

### 1. Verify each license from primary source
For every service we deploy or bundle:
- Check `LICENSE` / `LICENSE.txt` / `COPYING` in upstream repo root
- Check the `license` field in package.json / .csproj / project.json /
  equivalent if it exists
- Record the actual license text location in the audit table
- Flag any mismatch (readme says MIT but LICENSE is GPL, etc.)

### 2. Document per-service obligations
For each license + deployment-shape combination, write down what we
must do to comply:

**AGPLv3 (cookbook, _VS code, _DV code, Starlight-derived, _NF post-hardlight-style boundary)**
- Must distribute source of our version to anyone interacting with
  the service over a network
- Must preserve copyright + license notice
- Must mark modifications
- Derivative works must be AGPLv3
- Compliance plan: all our config files live in THIS public repo;
  link to this repo from each AGPL-deployed service's UI ("Source"
  link in footer pointing at github.com/azigler/vacation-station-14)

**MIT (SS14.Admin, SS14.MapServer/MapViewer, wizard-cogs, Robust.Cdn, RSIEdit, document-simu, SS14.Changelog, most upstream SS14 pre-AGPL code)**
- Must preserve copyright notice
- Must preserve permission notice
- Compliance plan: retain upstream `LICENSE` file in any clone/copy;
  add attribution to our website's /credits page and to the README
  attribution table

**CC-BY-SA 3.0 (most SS14 assets)**
- Must credit original author
- Must share modifications under same license
- Compliance plan: ensure `_VS` assets we derive from upstream
  retain credit; assets we author from scratch MAY be AGPL-compatible
  by licensing them CC-BY-SA 3.0 (matching upstream convention)

**CC-BY-NC-SA 3.0 (some SS14 assets)**
- NC = non-commercial only. We must NOT monetize these assets.
  Per user direction, no monetization is planned, so compliant by
  default.
- Compliance plan: document in LEGAL.md that assets under this
  license are explicitly non-commercial-use-only; if we ever change
  monetization stance, must audit + remove or replace NC assets
  first.

### 3. README.md licensing section (HardLight-style)
Add a section to our README.md following HardLight's format:

**3a. License boundary**
Pick a boundary commit. Candidates:
- The initial Flavor-A paragon commit (if we execute vs-ddu) — all
  VS14-authored content since then = AGPLv3
- Or our current initial-fork commit `062c0d7a` — our authored
  content since then = AGPLv3; inherited Delta-V / upstream content
  keeps its original license (MIT + AGPL mix per Delta-V's own
  LEGAL)

Probably second option for current state, first for post-paragon.

Wording template:
```
Content authored by VS14 contributors and committed to this
repository after commit <SHA> is licensed under the GNU Affero
General Public License version 3.0 unless otherwise annotated.

Content inherited from upstream forks retains its original license
(see attribution table below). Modifications to upstream-inherited
files are marked with inline `// VS` comments and are licensed under
AGPL-3.0.
```

**3b. Attribution table**
One row per upstream we import / inherit / cherry-pick from.
Columns: Subdirectory, Fork Name, Fork Repository, License, Our
mode (hard-fork / submodule / cherry-pick / deploy-as-is).

Example:
```
| Subdirectory | Fork | Repository | License | Mode |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `_DV` | Delta-V Station | DeltaV-Station/Delta-v | AGPL-3.0 | cherry-pick |
| `_NF` | Frontier Station | new-frontiers-14/frontier-station-14 | AGPL-3.0 + MIT | cherry-pick |
| `_VS` | Vacation Station 14 (this repo) | azigler/vacation-station-14 | AGPL-3.0 | authored |
| (engine) | RobustToolbox | space-wizards/RobustToolbox | MIT | submodule pin |
| (external/cookbook) | ss14-cookbook | arimah/ss14-cookbook | AGPL-3.0 | submodule + config |
| (external/admin) | SS14.Admin | space-wizards/SS14.Admin | MIT | submodule + config |
| ... | ... | ... | ... | ... |
```

**3c. Modification annotations**
Document the `// VS` / `// DV` / `// NF` / `// EE` inline-comment
convention. One sentence; maybe a small code block example.

### 4. Per-cherry-pick attribution discipline
Every cherry-picked commit must:
- Preserve the original author line (don't squash into "VS14 import")
- Add a `Co-Authored-By:` trailer for the original author if the
  cherry-pick needed any conflict-resolution edits
- Tag the subsystem / subdirectory it lands in (e.g. "cherry-pick:
  _NF/Bank from new-frontiers-14@abc1234")
- Reference the bead that scoped the cherry-pick
- State the upstream commit SHA so anyone can trace back

This discipline fully preserves license chains. A reader running
`git log --follow Content.Server/_NF/Bank/` will see original Frontier
authors alongside our conflict-resolution commits, each SHA traceable
to its upstream.

### 5. LEGAL.md updates
Extend existing LEGAL.md with:
- The HardLight-style license-boundary statement (cross-link to
  README)
- The full attribution table (README has a summary; LEGAL.md has
  the authoritative / extended version)
- Per-service deployment licensing obligations
- Contact for license questions (email + DMCA designated agent from
  vs-1ux)

### 6. Website /credits page
(Overlaps with vs-2dr website.) Rendered from LEGAL.md data or
`docs/community/credits.md`. Auto-generated or hand-curated —
either works if the data stays in sync.

### 7. Wizden OAuth TOS check
Confirm that Wizards Den explicitly permits fork / third-party use
of their identity provider. Usually documented in their infrastructure
docs or Discord. One paragraph in LEGAL.md citing their permission.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Every service in vs-19h's matrix has its license text location
      documented (file path + commit SHA)
- [ ] LEGAL.md extended with per-service compliance section
- [ ] AGPL-network-service compliance: "View Source" link visible from
      every AGPL-deployed service (cookbook especially)
- [ ] README.md has HardLight-style license-boundary statement
- [ ] README.md has HardLight-style per-upstream attribution table
- [ ] README.md documents the `// VS` / `// DV` / `// NF` comment
      convention
- [ ] All submodule LICENSE files intact at external/<name>/LICENSE
- [ ] Website /credits page drafted (vs-2dr depends on this bead's
      output)
- [ ] Cherry-pick commit discipline documented (author preservation
      + upstream SHA reference) in CLAUDE.md and /upstream-sync skill
- [ ] Trademark/branding sanity check complete; no conflicts
- [ ] Wizden OAuth TOS confirmed as permitting fork use
- [ ] docs/upstream-sync.md lists each upstream's license column

## Dependencies
- vs-2dr (website) — /credits page lives there
- vs-7ns (brand) — brand guide confirms we're not reusing protected
  marks
- vs-1ux (user-facing legal) — feeds this; TOS / privacy policy
  written against the actual license obligations
- vs-ddu (Flavor A) — if executed, the paragon boundary commit becomes
  the natural license-transition point

## Out of scope
- Hiring a lawyer for a full licensing opinion — start with boring
  due-diligence, engage counsel only if we hit ambiguity
- Re-licensing our own code (we're AGPL; keep it)
- Re-licensing the `_DV` / `_Starlight` / upstream-SS14 code we
  inherit (not ours to relicense)

## Notes
- AGPL "triggers" on public network interaction. Private / LAN
  deployment has no AGPL obligations. Hub-advertised public server =
  AGPL obligations apply.
- MIT upstream combined with our AGPL changes = the combined work is
  AGPL (more restrictive license wins). This is why our repo is
  effectively AGPL-distributed even though imported MIT code retains
  MIT licensing internally.
- Always preserve LICENSE files in copies. Deleting them is a
  violation regardless of our own license.
- HardLight's README is the model to study:
  https://github.com/HardLightSector/HardLight/blob/master/README.md
acceptance_criteria:

- LEGAL.md extended with per-service compliance section

- All submodule LICENSE files intact at external/<name>/LICENSE — not edited, not removed
- Website /credits page drafted (vs-2dr depends on this bead's output)

title: ops: postgres setup from day 1
description:
## Context
Level 5 hosting uses PostgreSQL instead of the default SQLite. Required for
SS14.Admin (which doesn't support SQLite) and for multi-instance deployments.
We want Postgres from day 1 so DB schema is production-shaped.

SS14 server runs migrations automatically on startup — DB user just needs
to own its database.

## Task
Install PostgreSQL, create vacation_station DB and user, configure SS14 to use
Postgres instead of SQLite, verify migrations run cleanly on first server start.

## Acceptance Criteria

### Installation
- [ ] setup.postgres.sh script that installs postgresql-16 (or 17) via apt
- [ ] systemctl enable postgresql
- [ ] postgresql listening on localhost:5432 (default)

### Database setup
- [ ] DB user `vs14` created with generated password (stored in password manager)
- [ ] Database `vacation_station` created, owned by `vs14`
- [ ] Verified: `psql -U vs14 -d vacation_station -c "select 1"`

### SS14 config
- [ ] instances/vacation-station/config.toml includes:
  [database]
  engine = "postgres"
  pg_host = "localhost"
  pg_port = 5432
  pg_database = "vacation_station"
  pg_username = "vs14"
  pg_password = "..."   # from password manager, NOT in repo
- [ ] First server start runs migrations cleanly (check logs: migrations applied N)
- [ ] Verify tables created: `psql -U vs14 -d vacation_station -c "\dt"`

### Access control
- [ ] pg_hba.conf restricts connections to localhost (default in most distros)
- [ ] PostgreSQL NOT exposed publicly (port 5432 bound to localhost or firewalled)
- [ ] Password generated with cryptographic entropy (openssl rand, not a dictionary word)

### Backup
- [ ] Cron or systemd timer for `pg_dump -Fc` nightly
- [ ] Backup destination documented (local for now, object storage later)
- [ ] Retention policy documented (e.g. 7 daily, 4 weekly)

### Connection pooling
- [ ] Postgres max_connections reviewed (default 100 usually fine for single instance)
- [ ] No PgBouncer needed initially (revisit if we scale)

### Documentation
- [ ] docs/OPERATIONS.md Postgres section: install, user/DB creation, config wiring,
  backup/restore procedures, migration to S3-compatible storage path
- [ ] Credential rotation procedure documented

title: ops: deploy SS14.Changelog webhook service for auto-generated changelogs
description:
## Context
SS14.Changelog (https://github.com/space-wizards/SS14.Changelog) is an
ASP.NET Core webhook receiver that auto-populates a repo's
`Changelog.yml` from `:cl:` blocks in merged PRs. SS14 server reads
that yml at startup and shows players a "what's new since last
connect" panel in-game.

MIT-licensed, ~36 commits, actively maintained by Wizden.

## Why file upfront (user direction)
Prefer setting this up before community PR traffic begins rather than
scrambling to add it mid-launch. When the first contributor's PR lands,
their changelog block should already auto-route to the in-game panel —
good community signal.

## Architecture

```
Contributor opens PR with :cl: block in description
           ↓
       PR merges to main
           ↓
GitHub webhook → https://hooks.vacation.<domain>/ss14-changelog/hook
           ↓
SS14.Changelog service parses :cl: from PR body
           ↓
Commits an update to Changelog.yml on main (via deploy SSH key)
           ↓
Watchdog picks up the content repo's new HEAD on next update cycle
           ↓
Game server reloads, players see the new changelog in-game
```

## Deployment shape — follows vs-19h submodule+config pattern

1. Submodule under `external/ss14-changelog/`:
   ```
   git submodule add https://github.com/space-wizards/SS14.Changelog external/ss14-changelog
   git config -f .gitmodules submodule.external/ss14-changelog.branch master
   git config -f .gitmodules submodule.external/ss14-changelog.ignore dirty
   ```
2. Configs under `ops/ss14-changelog/`:
   - `docker-compose.yml` — builds from `external/ss14-changelog/`,
     binds `127.0.0.1:<port>`, env-loaded secrets, mount for SSH key
   - `appsettings.Production.yml.example` — with:
     ```yaml
     ChangelogRepositories:
       - RepositoryUrl: git@github.com:azigler/vacation-station-14.git
         Branch: main
         ChangelogFilename: Resources/Changelog/Changelog.yml
         PrCommitMessage: ":memo: changelog: entry for PR #{0}"
         CommitterName: "VS14 Changelog Bot"
         CommitterEmail: "changelog-bot@vacation.<domain>"
         GitBranch: main
         SshKeyPath: "/run/secrets/changelog_deploy_key"
     GitHub:
       WebhookSecret: "<from env>"
     Serilog:
       WriteTo:
         - Name: Console
         - Name: GrafanaLoki
           Args:
             uri: "http://host.docker.internal:3100"
             labels:
               - key: app
                 value: ss14-changelog
     ```
   - `Caddyfile.block` — route `hooks.vacation.<domain>/ss14-changelog/`
     to `127.0.0.1:<port>`
   - Secret mount: deploy SSH key registered as a GitHub deploy key
     on our repo with `write:code` scope, stored at
     `/etc/vacation-station/changelog-deploy-key`

3. GitHub side:
   - Register a webhook on `azigler/vacation-station-14`:
     - Payload URL: `https://hooks.vacation.<domain>/ss14-changelog/hook`
     - Content type: `application/json`
     - Events: `Pull requests`, `Pushes`
     - Secret: matches `GitHub:WebhookSecret`
   - Add the deploy key (public half) to the repo's Deploy Keys with
     write access
   - Create the `ss14-changelog-bot` user account on GitHub (or use
     one we already have) for the committer identity

4. Game-server side:
   - Create `Resources/Changelog/` dir if not present
   - Seed `Changelog.yml` with an initial empty-but-valid YAML
   - Verify SS14 server reads our VS14 changelog file. Upstream default
     reads `Resources/Changelog/Changelog.yml` — confirm cvar if
     different path needed.

5. First-run test:
   - Open a test PR with a `:cl:` block in its body
   - Merge it
   - Confirm webhook fires (Caddy access log)
   - Confirm service commits the changelog update
   - Confirm in-game changelog panel shows the entry on next server start

## Contributor-facing convention — `:cl:` block
Document in `CONTRIBUTING.md` (and update `/commit` skill):
```
:cl:
- add: new entity X
- tweak: balanced Y
- fix: bug in Z
```
Categories: `add`, `remove`, `tweak`, `fix`. Admin-facing:
`VSADMIN:` prefix on admin-only changes.

We already use this convention in commit messages (our /commit skill
emits it). When the webhook service is live, PR descriptions also need
to carry the same block — clarify both in contributor docs.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] external/ss14-changelog/ submodule added
- [ ] ops/ss14-changelog/ configs committed
- [ ] Deploy key registered on repo
- [ ] Webhook registered on repo
- [ ] docker-compose stack running under systemd
- [ ] Caddy routing hooks subdomain
- [ ] Test PR merge triggers Changelog.yml update
- [ ] In-game changelog panel displays the new entry
- [ ] CONTRIBUTING.md documents the :cl: block expectation for PRs
- [ ] /commit skill cross-refs the PR-description :cl: workflow
- [ ] vs-3tq license audit row added (MIT, attribution preserved)

## Dependencies
- vs-2y8 (Caddy) — webhook needs HTTPS inbound from GitHub
- vs-19h (submodule convention established)

## Out of scope
- Per-category changelog filtering (upstream supports this; we can
  configure it but not here)
- Migration of historical commit :cl: blocks into Changelog.yml —
  starting fresh is easier
- Discord cross-post of changelog entries — separate bead, pairs with
  vs-2l2 Discord bot
notes: Post-Flavor-A: changelog file path is SS14 default Resources/Changelog/Changelog.yml (not Delta-V's DeltaVChangelog.yml). Update appsettings ChangelogFilename after vs-ddu Phase 1 lands.

title: feat: nurseshark frontend — reference pages + pro-tips + cross-links
description:
## Context

Child under vs-3il. Everything the user sees outside of the solver.
Consumes the JSON emitted by the data-pipeline bead.

## Scope

### Routes

- `/` — redirects to `/solver` (Rx) per vs-2wj's operator-first landing
  decision
- `/solver` — the Rx solver (handled in vs-2wj, not this bead)
- `/reagents` — full chemistry reference. Grid of cards (cookbook visual
  language) for every reagent; click a card to see the detail view with
  recipe + heal rates + OD threshold + interactions
- `/reagents/:id` — per-reagent detail view
- `/reactions` — full reaction browser (search, filter by temperature
  requirement / reactant / product)
- `/damage` — damage-type reference: per type, list every reagent + item
  that heals it, their rates, and the razorium-style hazards within the
  type. Also shows species modifiers (e.g. "Dionas take 50% more Heat")
- `/damage/:type` — per damage type drill-down
- `/species` — species biology cards: per species, damage modifiers,
  blood metabolism exceptions, gotchas from the guidebook-XML fold-in
- `/cryo` — cryo procedures page: cryoxadone / aloxadone / opporozidone
  / doxarubixadone + patient prep checklist + cryo-gas swap rules
- `/pro-tips` — renders `src/data/pro-tips.md` with damage-type
  grouping + `[verified]` / `[unverified]` / `[new]` tag filters
- `/about` — credits, license, Inspirations, version string from `meta.json`

### Components

- Reagent card (cookbook-parallel visual language)
- Reaction card (reactant arrow product display, temperature badge
  when minTemp > 0)
- Damage-type badge (color-coded per category: brute, burn, toxin, etc.)
- Species badge (icon + name)
- Search bar (global — appears in nav; fuzzy-matches across all
  reagents + reactions + species + damage types)
- Pro-tip callout (yellow for `[unverified]`, green for `[verified]`,
  blue for `[new]`)
- Copy-label button (reusable across reagent detail, solver output,
  planner output; consistent label format)

### Global UX

- Keyboard shortcuts (per the app-wide scheme): `/` focus search,
  `g` + letter jumps to section (e.g. `g r` reagents, `g d` damage,
  `g s` solver), `esc` closes any modal
- Dark theme default (SS14 is played at night; most medics play
  in dim environments; matches cookbook)
- Responsive: usable in a narrow window alongside the game client

### Deep-links into sibling VS14 tools

- Per-reagent card: "Details in Guidebook" link to
  `/guidebook/#<reagent-id>` (stretch — depends on guidebook
  anchor format)
- Reaction involving a foodstuff reagent: link to `/cookbook/` search
  for that ingredient (stretch)

## Dependencies

- Blocks on data-pipeline bead (needs the JSON output to consume)
- Sibling to vs-2wj solver bead (shares the search bar component + the
  reagent detail component)

## Acceptance

- [ ] All routes render (even with empty placeholder data)
- [ ] `/` redirects to `/solver`
- [ ] Reagent card grid renders from `reagents.json` with sprites from
      `sprites.png` + `sprites_manifest.json`
- [ ] Reaction browser supports filter by reactant / product / min temp
- [ ] Damage page cross-references every reagent that heals each type
- [ ] Species page surfaces the guidebook notes as readable text
- [ ] Pro-tips page renders the markdown with tag filters
- [ ] Keyboard shortcuts implemented
- [ ] Responsive at 400px width (minimum dev window size)
- [ ] Vitest snapshot tests for each route's render

## Out of scope

- Data editing / admin UI (read-only reference tool)
- User accounts (no backend)
- Server-side rendering (static SPA)
close_reason: Frontend shipped at nurseshark 7c5952f. All 10 routes render (/ redirect → /solver, /reagents grid + detail, /reactions browser, /damage index + drill-down with both direct-heal + group-via-heal perspectives, /species with collapsible guidebook notes, /cryo with chem cards + pro-tips fold-in, /pro-tips with tag-filter chips, /about with meta). 35 Vitest tests pass. Bundle 215KB JS / 70KB gzip, 3.2MB total dist including sprites. Fluent resolution via build-time pipeline extension (resolve-fluent.ts emits 65KB fluent.json covering 953 keys). Shared primitives (ReagentCard, ReagentDetail, SearchBar, CopyLabelButton, ProTipCallout, DamageBadge, SpeciesBadge) ready for vs-2wj to reuse in solver output. SolverPage.tsx has computeMix() stub clearly marked; signature in src/types.ts. Unblocks vs-2wj + vs-ygn.

title: ops: brand identity — logo, palette, fonts, brand guide
description:
## Context
Website (vs-2dr), Discord (vs-2l2), hub listing (vs-17n), launcher
browser entry, business-card social media posts — all need a
consistent visual identity. Right now VS14 has:
- A name ("Vacation Station 14")
- A hard-fork lineage
- Zero visual distinction

An unbranded server at hub launch looks amateurish even if the ops
are solid. Opposite is true too: a considered brand signals "these
people take this seriously" and attracts a better caliber of player
and contributor.

## Task
1. **Naming / positioning** (works with vs-3e3):
   - Tagline (1 sentence) — what IS VS14
   - Elevator pitch (3 sentences) — for the hub browser + website hero
2. **Logo / wordmark**:
   - Primary logo with theme (vacation? station? laid-back RP?) —
     distinct from upstream SS14's iconic atom logo
   - Monochrome variant for small-space use
   - Favicon (16×16, 32×32)
   - Discord server icon (512×512)
   - Avatar for launcher listing
3. **Color palette**:
   - Primary + secondary brand colors
   - Accent color (for CTAs and action UI)
   - Neutral palette for surfaces + text
   - Dark mode variant (most SS14 players live in terminal-black UIs;
     mirror that expectation)
4. **Typography**:
   - Display font (hero, headers) — distinct but readable
   - Body font (content) — web-performant, high legibility
   - Mono font for code / launcher instructions (match SS14's
     in-game mono vibe)
5. **Brand guide doc** at `docs/community/brand.md`:
   - Logo usage rules (don't stretch, don't recolor, minimum sizes)
   - Color hex codes + semantic names
   - Type scale
   - Tone of voice (matches vs-3e3 positioning — see vs-3e3 content
     for the written side)
   - Example usage: website hero, discord channel icon, launcher card
6. **Asset files**:
   - SVG source files (Figma or Affinity Designer source exported)
   - Raster exports at standard sizes
   - Committed to `assets/brand/` at repo root

## Acceptance
- [ ] Logo (primary + monochrome) + favicon
- [ ] Color palette documented with hex codes
- [ ] Font choices documented
- [ ] Brand guide committed as `docs/community/brand.md`
- [ ] All source + exported assets under `assets/brand/`
- [ ] Website (vs-2dr), Discord (vs-2l2), hub listing (vs-17n) all
      consuming the same assets

## Dependencies
- Everything visual blocks on this: website Phase 1 can ship with
  placeholder branding but public launch (vs-17n hub flip) really
  wants real brand

## Skills / budget
This is a design task. Options:
- DIY if you have the chops / tools
- Community contributor (artist in the SS14 space — many exist)
- Paid designer ($300-1500 for logo+palette+guide typical)
Pick based on time + budget + quality target.

## Out of scope
- Merch / promo materials (t-shirts, stickers) — separate ask if the
  community ever gets big enough to want them
- In-game skins / cosmetics (we said no monetization; if we ever do
  donator-visible cosmetics, they'd inherit this brand)

## Notes
- Don't overthink v1. Ship a "just good enough" brand and evolve.
  Zero brand > amateur-hour brand; mid brand > stalled-waiting-for-
  perfect brand.

## 2026-05-03 — Aesthetic direction locked: retro pixel-art + CRT bezel

After two days of iteration on a Frutiger Aero × Silicon Dreams
